The agents move through the doorway into the adjacent building. A fallen cupboard blocks the entrance. Burr pulls on it, his hands slip, and he falls backward onto broken glass, a shard cutting into the back of his right thigh. Together they work the cupboard forward enough for the door to swing open.
Inside, a dark hallway leads to a dilapidated dining hall with broken tables, mildewed tablecloths, and dust. Two doors sit in the hallway: a metal door with a glass circular window leading to the kitchen, and a peeling wooden door leading to a staircase blocked by a metal gate. Beyond, curtained windows overlook an empty street lined with broken cars, dark buildings, and trash bags. The front door is locked.
A light flickers behind them once, quick and faint. Burr runs down the stairs, fires a round through the window, and jumps through, his right leg catching on glass as he lands. He sustains a calf cut from the glass and a laceration from the landing. Pug follows more carefully and clears the window without injury.
A dark silhouette rushes past the metal door inside. Burr calls out. No response. Another figure crosses past the back door. Outnumbered and with unknown numbers still moving, the agents flee in the opposite direction of the alley.

The agents approach a depowered storefront identifiable only by its faded neon sign: a pair of skis and a beanie above the words Everbright Outlet. Inside, mannequin stands lie fallen and stripped, and most shelves have been ransacked. Burr takes the lead, gun drawn, scanning the darkness.

Tearing fabric from his pant leg and wrapping it around a broken piece of pallet wood, he fashions an improvised torch. It takes a couple tries and a splash of gasoline from a leaking container, but it catches. Black smoke curls upward. They have light.
Further in they find a red and white traveler duffel, empty and intact. Medical supplies appear: alcohol wipes, burn gel packets, a roll of aluminum-foam splints, water purification tablets. A bundle of paracord, a foldable shovel, two water-resistant ponchos, and two full sleeping bags join the haul. Burr loads everything into the duffel and straps the sleeping bags to his pack. They collect roughly half a liter of gasoline from the leaking container into a plastic bag.
As they backtrack through the shelving maze, something shuffles outside.

Snapshot
Summary
As the agents backtrack through the shelving maze, the plastic bag holding the gasoline melts through. Fuel begins to seep across the floor. Burr runs forward, sets the bag alight, and hurls the gasoline-filled sleeping bag out the entrance. A small fireball erupts on the pavement. Two sets of footsteps scramble away in panic. Burr yells out, demanding that whoever is out there state their intention. Silence follows. He bluffs about a man on the floor above with a gun. More footsteps skitter and run. One figure remains.
Burr moves outside, takes cover behind cars, and peers toward a slim alleyway. A shoe tip is visible behind a dumpster. A faint metallic thumping echoes against the dark. As Burr approaches, the shoe pulls back into concealment and the thumping intensifies. A figure in dark rags springs from behind the dumpster, a flash of metal in hand. Burr barges forward, catches the wrist, and flips the man over his shoulder. He stomps down on the man’s neck. A sickening crunch. Gurgling. The figure goes still. A pocket knife clatters onto the pavement. Burr pockets it and walks out.
They evaluate their options. Three paths branch ahead. One feels cold and wet with dripping condensation. One is lined with refuse and black tarps. One is narrow but familiar. They choose the cold branch. The air grows thick and moist, the chill settling deep. They don their ponchos, thin reflective material covering them from the dripping overhead, and press on.

A bell jingles overhead as they step in. The store is still.
Burr gathers three cans of beef soup, an apple juice carton, and an orange juice carton from the shelves. Pug searches behind the cashier counter and finds a sticky note with the number 9874 and a notepad with a staff warning advising employees not to disturb the Manager in the back rooms. He draws his gun and heads through the store. Burr dips a finger into an open green carton. The liquid irritates his skin, leaving the tip of his pinky reddened. He dries it off and the burning stops, but the irritation lingers.
No threats emerge. They move on toward the management level.

Snapshot
Summary
The agents head toward the back of the market. Pug spots a door labeled with a strip of white electrical tape, the words Managers Ofice written in black marker. Burr notices a damaged spot on the wall beside the door where something was apparently removed.
Inside, the room is dark. The floor is slick with water. Burr feels along the wall and finds a light switch with an unusual gap behind the outlet, as if something could reach past it into the wall. Pug moves to the switch and flicks it on. Wires trail from the switch to metal poles at the edges of the room, touching into the water below. A jolt of electricity arcs through the room. Pug, still wearing shoes, is partially insulated, but enough current passes through to seize his muscles and send a flash of pain through him. The lights go out. From the front of the store, a bell jingles.
Burr charges forward toward a humanoid silhouette by the door, a figure in a hood. An animalistic screech answers his approach. The creature drops to the floor and scurries into the darkness, knocking over shelves and throwing cans as it moves. One can of beef stew cracks open on impact. Burr sets down his gear and advances, cornering the creature in the dark. It wheezes, coughs, and forces out broken words: “S.. top.. Leave.. p.. ease..”
Burr tells it to return to the office. The creature rustles, shuffles across the tile, and retreats into the Managers Ofice. The door clicks shut. After a moment, the lights flicker back on. Soft wheezing and coughing come from behind the door. No further engagement.

Snapshot
Summary
The agents follow the misty path until a crash draws them to a nearby residential building. The door swings open easily, revealing a small lobby with a reception desk, a hallway, and a staircase leading up. Pug takes a moment to rest while Burr ascends the spiral stairs to investigate the second floor.
The upstairs hallway has rooms on either side. The first door on the right is locked, so Burr kicks the mechanism loose. The door swings open, and a moment later, glass shatters in the room beyond. Investigating the dark room, Burr finds it empty and undisturbed, so he moves to the next door and kicks it open. The room inside is illuminated. Two shots ring out, the bullets hitting the wall behind him. Burr returns fire with two shots of his own, and shots come back, one hitting the wall and one the doorframe. He pushes away, firing once more as he moves, crashing backward through the wall in the process, leaving a man-sized hole with himself partially lodged in it. No more shots follow.
They regroup at the doorway of the second room. Inside is a fallen wardrobe that had been shoved in a poor attempt to block the door, a shattered vase, and a trail of blood across the floor. A man in a charcoal grey suit sits against the wall, a red tie loosened around his neck, one hand clutching his chest and the other repeatedly pulling the trigger of an empty handgun. He does not notice them at first. When he does, he swings the gun toward them, still trying to fire, desperation and confusion on his face.
Burr approaches. The man chokes out a name, Jasper, but cannot say more. He does not know who he works for. He pleads, says he does not want to die, speaks of people coming, though he cannot say who. The light fades from his eyes as he slips away. Burr lays him on the bed and places his handgun in his hands.
On the bedside table, a pair of brass knuckles. Burr pockets them. Pug takes Jasper’s identification from his jacket. They head back outside.

Snapshot
Summary
The agents step into the lobby, preparing to head back outside. The sound of a door opening stops them. Footsteps file in from the far end of the building, multiple sets. A voice calls out: keep it careful, the target is here, an easy job, do not get clipped like the others.
Pug grabs a fire extinguisher from near the lounge chairs. They stack up on opposite sides of the wall as the footsteps draw closer. Doorknobs jingle. Some doors open, steps breaking off from the group. When they cross into the planned kill zone, Pug rounds the corner and throws the fire extinguisher toward them. One of them yells, and the shot goes through the extinguisher. It ruptures, spraying foam and gas across the corridor, the pressurized contents spinning and hissing, creating a makeshift smokescreen.
Burr advances into the fog. Three vague figures. They are covering their eyes, foam splattered across them, disoriented. Burr reaches the first man before he registers the threat. The shovel spears forward, crushing his nose into his face, the cartilage cracking as his head knocks backward into a doorframe. He screams. The shovel comes down on his foot, then a palm strike to his broken nose. He crumples to his knees, groaning.
Pug fires a shot from Burr’s handgun at the figures further down the hall. The trigger locks after one round. He tosses Burr’s gun aside and pulls his own sidearm, pulling back behind the wall.
One of the figures further back cries out, stumbling into the third man, then turns and charges down the hallway. The third man falls back into a doorframe.
Burr pushes forward, ignoring the charging man for the moment, advancing on the figure in the doorframe. His opponent raises a medium-length rod or baton. Burr feints, then switches at the last second. The blow lands on the man’s head, a glancing strike that draws blood and stuns him. A kick catches the side of his knee. Not broken, but his leg gives out and he falls. The shovel slams down into his neck, crunching through. The man’s breath stops mid-beat. Burr picks up the fallen pipe. Doorframe Raider C is dead.
The charging man barrels forward, yelling, ducking for a tackle. Burr swings the pipe, cracking it against the side of his head. He goes limp mid-tackle, his body still slamming into Burr’s leg and jostling him.
From behind, the first man stirs, trying to pick himself up, still holding a folding knife. Pug rushes forward and pistol-whips him, cracking him across the head with the base of the gun. His eyes roll back as he slumps down, alive but out of the fight.
Pug fires a shot from his own handgun at the fleeing figure sprinting past. The bullet passes through him. He staggers, drops his wrench, keeps running. He rounds the corner and disappears outside.
Burr advances further down the hall. Two men wait at the end. One is hooded, face masked, holding a kitchen knife. The other is larger, wearing a thick canvas duster over a blue stab-proof vest, hands bare. The larger man shouts at them. Burr answers that they are dead men.
Burr charges the knife-wielder. He throws the pipe, cracking the man’s forearm and glancing off his head. With his hands raised to protect his head, the shovel strikes his side. Ribs crack. The larger man rushes in with a punch to the side of Burr’s head, rocking him. Burr follows through, striking the knife-wielder in the groin. His face contorts and he crumples into the wall, a silent scream caught in his throat before Burr finishes him. Hooded Raider D is dead.
The larger man takes advantage of Burr’s position and drives a jab into his lower back. Burr locks his arm, twists. The man shoulders him into the wall, shoving back. Burr pushes off, throws him to the ground, mounts him. The shovel and brass knuckles come down again and again. The man’s arms go up to resist, but Burr keeps swinging, the metal folding mechanism snapping under the force, until what remains of his face is a broken, bloody mess. Cocky Raider Leader is dead.
After the fighting, the agents move through the fallen, finishing off those still alive. Pug finishes Resilient Raider A. Burr finishes Charging Raider E and ensures Hooded Raider D is gone. Then they begin looting. Pug takes the folding knife from Resilient Raider A, the kitchen knife from Hooded Raider D, and Burr passes him the pocket knife. Burr takes the leader’s thick canvas duster, blue stab-proof vest, and suede combat boots, along with cargo pants from one of the other men. Inside the thick canvas duster pocket, a folded note. Pug reads it: someone heard a shot nearby and wants the target brought back alive. It is signed with a single letter, S.
The exhaustion of the day settles over them. They pick separate rooms, de-gear, and fall asleep.

Snapshot
Summary
The agents settle into separate rooms and drift off, the exhaustion of the day pulling them under. Burr wakes to the sound of floorboards creaking from the far end of the hallway. Heavy, lopsided footsteps, each step landing with a pronounced limp. The sound draws closer, stopping in front of his door.
A red glow seeps under the doorframe, illuminating the room. A mechanical jostle, gears turning. The hiss of pressurized steam. Then tearing flesh and bubbling liquid, the red glow intensifying. A cacophony of similar sounds from further down the hall as other pairs of footsteps arrive. The commotion lasts less than a minute before the footsteps recede as a group and the hallway falls silent.
They try to return to sleep. The footsteps return. Then again. Three waves in total, each time the building groaning with the weight of whatever passes through. After the third wave, the sounds do not come back. The silence holds.
Hours later, Burr’s stomach growls. He stirs, gets dressed. The morning light is dim through the grime-streaked windows. When they open the door, the hallway is spotless. No blood. No debris. No bodies. No sign that any violence occurred the night before.
The full night’s rest allows their bodies to mend. Burr’s head clears from the earlier impacts. Pug’s accumulated bruising fades. The deeper wounds on Burr’s thigh and calf begin to close, the plastic wrap and string dressing finally doing its work undisturbed.

Snapshot
Summary
The agents wake naturally, the morning light filtering through grime-streaked windows. Burr’s stomach growls. They don their gear and step into the hall, finding it spotless. No bodies. No blood. No sign of the violence from the night before.
They head outside. Burr wears his poncho; Pug’s is packed in the duffel. Dew droplets fall from the rooftops, sliding off Burr’s poncho as they walk. A drop lands on Pug’s exposed head. A light, acidic burning sets in across his scalp. He pulls the poncho from the duffel and puts it on, the stinging fading as the remaining dew in his hair dries.
The streets look different in the daylight. The path twists and turns until a familiar sight appears: a hanging lit lantern between two buildings, marked with symbols neither agent can decipher. The building beneath it is small, with a closed reed window set into the wall like a bank teller booth. A bell sits on the shelf beneath the lantern. Burr rings it.
The reed window slides up. A small man sits behind it, shifty-eyed, wearing a black uniform like a bellhop. He speaks first in a language they do not understand, then switches: are they here for directions?
Burr asks about food. The man trades information for information. Burr sets down the alcohol wipes. The man inspects them, considers, then asks about a fallen feather, a shooting nearby. Burr tells him about the building where they found Jasper. Something stirs behind the man, writing. A thin brown tail reaches over his shoulder and places a sealed envelope in his hand. The man pushes it forward. Directions to food, accurate for the next hour.
Burr asks about weapons. The man tilts his head, studies what they have. Paracord is inspected and returned. Burn gel is accepted. The tail writes again. A second sealed envelope is produced: directions to a weapon source, valid for one day if they return to this spot.
The agents step away, having paid their fee of burn gel, alcohol wipes, and information.

Snapshot
Summary
The rain bears down hard, falling between the shanty roofs and makeshift shelters, soaking through the duffel strapped to Burr’s back. They follow the directions backward, retracing their route to the Station. But the streets do not cooperate. A curve that should bend left bends right instead. A familiar street leads back to the restaurant. They loop, double back, and eventually abandon the directions entirely, pushing forward by instinct.
Rounding a corner, they spot three figures huddled under a scrap metal awning. Ratty hoods, two on the right, one on the left, sharing a smoke. Behind them, the familiar glow of the lantern on the wall.
Burr moves forward without slowing. One of them steps out, hand raised to stop them. Burr runs past. The other two reach for weapons, but the agents are already through, brazen and uncaring, leaving the men standing dumbfounded.
The Station is ahead. The reed window slides open, but a different face sits behind it, shifty-eyed, in the same bellhop uniform. He confirms the weapon directions are still valid. All stations share the same origin. Pug opens the envelope. Inside, a shorter set of instructions: a U-turn, a right turn, a rectangle with a small circle like a door.
They turn to leave. The three men are coming down the street behind them, following. The right alleyway waits past them.
The men focus on Pug. One brandishes a small ball-peen hammer, calling him smoothskin. Burr pulls out the brass knuckles. They stop, reassessing. Pug draws the E.G.O. handgun. They stare at it, confused, exchanging glances. The agents holster their weapons. The men back up, calling Pug baby bottom, before turning and running.
The agents follow the new directions. The mist and rain thin as the alley stretches forward. Eventually, a metal sheet door appears, set into a makeshift barricade. This is the place.

The metal door swings open. Warmer, drier air washes over them, a stark contrast to the rain-soaked district behind them. They step through. The door closes and melts into the wall behind them, seamless, no handle on this side. There is no going back.
The street ahead is lined with abandoned cars, stripped to their frames, components long scavenged. Across the street, a man in ragtag clothing catches sight of them. He wears a shiny grey vest, a construction helmet, sportswear kneepads, and a crowbar hangs at his hip.
He calls out, voice wary. Who are they? Are they with the Stray Dogs?
The confusion in their answers gives him pause. He looks at them, concerned. Head injury? It is not safe out here. Come, follow me.

Snapshot
Summary
The guide leads them to a cluster of three apartment buildings forming a U-shape, the open side sealed by a large sheet metal gate. Scaffolding rises into makeshift ramparts above it. A figure atop the scaffolding gestures, and a chainlink fence door slides open.
Inside is a small community. Farmer’s market stalls line the courtyard. A group exercises in formation, led by an instructor. Green canvassed medical tents stand at the far end, people moving between them.
Welcome to the Community, the guide says. Better than whatever shithole you came from.
Four more guards in makeshift armor approach and surround them. The guide apologizes. They need to hold onto the weapons. Just a safety reason. Pug shifts one of his handguns deeper into the duster pocket. The civilian who arrives with the box for Burr’s weapons is calm, routine. Burr sets down his bags and his hands go to the duffel straps. As he lifts them, something in his leg gives. Blood oozes from the old wound. His face goes pale and he crumples to the ground. Two guards and the civilian catch him and carry him toward the medical tents.
The guide steps between Pug and the stretcher. Hold fast, rockstar. Your friend is in good care. Show us the same trust.
He pats Pug down personally, more experienced than the civilian, checking sleeves and pockets. He finds the outline of the E.G.O. handgun in the duster. He reaches in and pulls it out. His eyes widen. He pales. He looks at the gun, then at Pug, then tucks it into his own jacket.
We will talk about this, he says. First, medical help. You will meet with Ben.
The guide breaks off toward the middle apartment complex, the gun with him.
In the medical tent, the doctors have already begun work on Burr. His leg has been exposed, the thigh laceration opened and bleeding freely. They disinfect it with vodka and suture the wound closed. A small bandage is wrapped around his head.
One of the doctors offers Pug a shot of vodka and asks what is wrong with his body. Pug mentions his head. The doctor runs through vision tests, switching between alphabet charts until Pug can read one. He shines a light in his eyes. He finds nothing wrong. He offers Pug a key to C Building, Room 314. Get some rest, he says. The pill is for your friend, when he wakes, before bed.
Pug and the doctor carry Burr up three flights of stairs to the room. It is barebones but practical: a small kitchen, a bedroom with two single beds, a bathroom, and a center room. Pug asks for a marker. While the doctor is distracted, he strips Burr’s shirt and draws marks across his torso to mimic kidney surgery scars.
The doctor leaves. Pug settles in to rest.

Snapshot
Summary
Burr wakes in a cold, empty tub. Shirtless, no gear. Dashes of marker across his lower abdomen like surgical indicators. Newly added sutures ache in his leg. Proper bandaging wraps around his head. The last thing he remembers is dropping unconscious in an unfamiliar camp after giving up his weapons.
He clambers out of the tub and steps into the living room. Pug is lounging on the couch. They exchange banter about kidneys and Pug’s reluctance to tell the truth about what happened while Burr was out. Burr storms off angrily down the hall. Pug catches up and offers him a healing pill. Burr takes it and swallows.
They head for the elevator. The pain in Burr’s head and leg begins to fade. The elevator does not arrive. After a moment of waiting, Burr decides to take the stairs. Pug follows. They descend floor after floor.
On the landing between the second floor and the ground, someone is coming up. Burr brushes past them too quickly. A teenage boy, small and meek, steps back to get out of the way and drops a small pouch on the floor. Burr picks it up and hands it back, apologizing. The boy mutters thanks in a language Burr does not quite recognise. They continue down.
At the ground floor they step outside. The community is quieter now, shops closing or preparing to. The training session has finished and the trainee guards are gone. The medical tents remain busy with a new patient. They head over.
Inside they find the two doctors who worked on Burr. The darker, bald man introduces himself as Hakeem, head of medical. He gestures to a row of cubbies. Burr’s gear is on the right, bottom row. Burr reclaims his suede combat boots and blue stab-proof vest.
At Pug’s inquiry, Hakeem explains the community’s structure. Dux, the one who brought them in, is leader of the guards. The founder is no longer with them. His friend Ben has taken up a similar role. Hakeem points to Building B, the middle residential building. Ben can be found on the top floor. Dux may be there too.
Passing through the courtyard, Pug glances at the patient on the medical table. A young woman in a hooded jacket, brown hair, bandages around her forehead and one eye. Unconscious. The other doctor finishes wrapping her ankle in gauze.
They head to Building B and stand at the bottom of the stairs. Ten flights, give or take. Burr begins the ascent. The stairs are harder going up than they were coming down. The sutures in his leg strain and burn even through the medication. Halfway to the second floor he realises Pug is not behind him. He continues alone, floor after floor, pushing through the pain, staving off the lactic acid building in his legs.
He reaches the top floor. Opens the door to the hallway. Pug is leaning against the wall. He took the elevator.

Snapshot
Summary
The door opens into a large apartment room converted into a gathering space. Several tables pushed together form a central area. Two men are inside.
One wears a white business shirt with rolled sleeves, dark aviator shades, bald. The other looks like a cross between a scientist and a punk rock musician, sickly pale with grime-covered skin, a lab coat with studded shoulders and pins scattered across it, grimy black hair at neck length, sunken eyes with a playful look. His arms are the most prominent feature. His right arm from the shoulder down is a bionic prosthetic with black and red decals, the lab coat cut away at the shoulder. His left arm from elbow to hand is also prosthetic but more mechanical, the hand compact with several embedded tools like a swiss army knife.
The scientist speaks first with an awkward joking voice, trying to break the ice. He says he was just wrapping up. He puts down a folder in front of the man in the shades, who does not look at it. As he heads out he does finger guns towards the man. Pritel, keep up the doses, everything A-okay. The man thanks him. Koller. The scientist misjudges the distance, stumbles as he rights himself and squeezes between the two agents on his way out, apologising and waving back at them. He leaves toward the elevator.
The man in the aviators gestures to the seats. He is Ben. He just helps run things around here. He calls it the Community.
Ben explains that their weapons are in the guardhouse on the ground floor. Tenants get them back when they head out. Not kept from them, just for safety.
He pulls out the confiscated gun and examines it by the barrel, not touching the grip or trigger. He reaches under his desk and pulls out another pistol. He puts it back. He knows they do not know where or who they are. He has seen it before, in a sense. This stays secret between them.
He will not share what he knows about them to others. They are still in District 12. Backstreets. Sections have been sectioned and sealed. The only known ways into the Nest have been taken over by Syndicates. They are fallen feathers. Ex-employees of the Wing that governed this District. Not the normal kind. They worked for the ones who called the shots.
After the Wing fell, everything fell apart. All the facilities entombed themselves and reduced themselves to rubble. They should not be alive, but they are. And so are others. People want answers and are willing to pay for anyone who might have them. This extends to fallen feathers.
Ben holds up the gun by the barrel. He is willing to trust them. But he needs their help first before they get it back.
There is a group expanding territory west of the Community. They have been starting trouble. Residents are scared to head out. Recently they took over a small warehouse district where some of the Community’s people scavenge. It would be good to get it back. Show the people they can be relied on.
While they are helping out, the Community’s resources are their resources. Ben mentions that a sword would be difficult but not impossible to acquire. Koller is not part of the Community but offers his services to them. Ben can give directions to his office or let him know they are looking for him.
He sends them off. Fruitful evening. Meet Dux at the guardhouse downstairs to get geared up. Get a good night’s rest first, then set out in the morning. You boys sleep tight. Do not let the sweepers bite.
They return to their room in Building C and sleep through the night. The creatures of the night pass through outside, sweeping through the residential buildings, the medical tents, the stalls. Three times. Between each pass they drift back to sleep.

Snapshot
Summary
Ahead of the group, Kellestine speedwalks to catch up and confront Burr about whatever was said about his bald head. He turns back to glare. People like Burr just do not get it. Bald is awesome. He shines, draws attention. Burr’s drab cut only attracts flies.
Burr mentions the glint gives away position to snipers. Kellestine pauses, thinks about it, then brushes it off. No one is hitting him. He speeds ahead and does a little sidestep back and forth, ducking his head in a dodge demonstration. He hits his head into Burr’s, trips on his own feet, and falls to the ground. He scrambles back up. You see that? Burr missed. He had to hit into him. Burr is lucky.
Kellestine claims he was a killer back before the fall. Guys coming at him in droves, stumbling off themselves trying to get at him. He quiets down after that, thinking. He tells Burr to worry about himself. He will be fine. They will piss themselves running. Do not get yourself killed.
Burr and Kellestine share a moment. Kellestine sees it in Burr. You are a killa alright. Then he asks if Burr has ever thought about going bald. He knocks on his helmet. That is why he hides the shine for now. Gotta be careful. Burr should have grabbed a helmet too.
Behind them, Pug walks with Chert. She explains that after she ate, the head guard called her and Kellestine in. Told them they could stay but there was work to do. Scavenge food from the warehouse. Expect trouble. She arrived yesterday, does not remember much. Fell and hit her head, woke up here. She thought she was in some rip clinic about to meet her end. But they helped her. She feels it is only right to do this job before deciding whether to stay.
She asks about Pug and Burr. They seem to know each other. Can Pug rely on him? Pug reassures her. She lightens up. She is not sure how well she can get along with Kellestine. She is glad Pug and Burr are here. Maybe they will have meat for dinner.
Ahead, the warehouse district comes into view. The two forward figures stop and wait. The backline catches up.

Snapshot
Summary
Kellestine looks over at Burr. What is the plan, Bossman? He draws his tire iron, giving distance but following. Pug equips a knife and follows suit, Chert at the rear. The small trek to the warehouse door is uneventful.
The metal door has small holes at eye level. Peeking through, the interior is dim, lit only by roof windows. Movement inside, some of it in the dark spots. At least two individuals confirmed: one carrying a small box of cans, the other walking and looking around.
Burr pulls open the door. It is unlocked. He swings it open and charges. The man with the cans drops the box and tries to run, stumbling. Burr catches him, grabbing him by the knee and neck, lifting him. The man panics and yells for help.
Before Burr can interrogate him, the other man grabs a broken pallet piece and charges. Kellestine and Chert hang back near the door. The older man yells, telling Burr to get off him. Burr grabs him by the ankles, tosses him into the younger man. They crash to the floor together.
Burr begins swinging with his brass knuckles. The two men try to fight back but the barrage overwhelms them. Most hits land. Kellestine watches in shock, focused on the carnage.
Meanwhile, Pug takes Chert to the other warehouse to watch for reinforcements. Peeking through the door, people are mobilizing inside. Men yell at each other, throw weapons around, some run away.
Burr stops swinging. The two men are battered and beaten but alive. The older one pleads between ragged breaths. Not his boy. Please. They are from a street further in. Burr can take what he wants.
Pug opens the door. A man with a pipe immediately charges. Pug throws the kitchen knife at his head. The knife, unbalanced and not intended for throwing, does not fly true. The man raises his arm to block. The knife stabs into his arm, puncturing his jacket, then falls and clatters to the floor.
The man charges, swinging downward. Pug sidesteps. The swing misses and carries toward Chert. She squeaks and raises her baseball bat, blocking the blow but getting knocked back. Pug pulls a rusted knife and stabs into the man’s throat. The tang breaks. The handle comes off. The blade stays lodged in his throat as he crumples to the floor.
One of the other armed men yells. They killed Jerry. Stay back. He holds up a crowbar as a deterrent. A girl behind him holds a boxcutter.
Burr lets the two beaten men go. The older one struggles up, the younger helping him hobble and limp away.
Pug retrieves the kitchen knife from the floor and steps past the dying man. Chert follows. They search the third warehouse. Empty.
They head back to the first warehouse. No sign of Kellestine. Burr yells. No reply. Moving deeper, they find an ajar door to a non-storage area. A hallway. At the end of one corridor, a body on the floor. Another door slightly ajar to the right. Heavy, labored breathing.
Pug checks the body. A young man, blunt force trauma to the head. Unconscious or dead. Burr kicks open the door. The breathing quickens, defensive. Slouched in the corner, one hand on a tire iron, is Kellestine.
He is shaken. Two of them came through the back. He killed one. One struck him and ran. He stands with difficulty. Burr talks him through it. Kellestine steadies himself.
They find the unconscious man is still alive. Burr finds a bundle of wire, a power cable, and ties him up. Pug and Chert find rope from cargo crates. They crack open crates. Chicken broth. Green beans. Peaches in syrup. Green peas. They load what they can carry onto small pallets.
Four of them head outside. Three small crates of loot and a prisoner.

Snapshot
Summary
After the plan is settled, the three of them head back toward the Community, leaving Burr behind to recon the reinforcements. The group the man had called the Death’s Head.
Chert is initially worried about leaving one of their own behind, but the success of the mission brightens her. She cannot believe it went so smoothly. A bit more people than expected, but thanks to them it went well. A good amount of supplies. Shame about the lack of meat, though.
She thinks she might ask to stay at the Community permanently. Volunteer for kitchen work. This kind of work feels too dangerous.
Kellestine tries to puff out his chest but loses balance under the crates, righting himself. Bossman sees potential in him. He is going to live up to it. Next mission, they can count on him.
From the alleyway he sits in, Burr sees a large group coming down the road. About a dozen men. Most wear some kind of leathers, white shirts, jeans, leather vests, some with sleeves and some without. Three wear kneepads and boots with small half masks reaching their nose. Three are heavily armored in boots, leather pants, shoulderpads, and gloves, wearing road goggles and motorcycle helmets. Their weapons match what the Community uses: tire irons, wrenches, claw hammers. One man has a pool stick.
A dozen armed men is too many. Burr turns to leave as they begin forming a perimeter around the street, keeping an eye on each other, sending others to filter into the warehouses. They yell at each other with basic communication.
One calls him a pussy as he runs. He catches up to the others. Several of the Death’s Head notice but do not give chase.

Snapshot
Summary
The three of them are about three-quarters of the way to the Community when two figures step out of an alleyway and block the path ahead. One toys with a rusty knife. The other cracks his neck, a metal pipe gripped in his hand. Hand over the supplies, and no one gets hurt.
They set down the boxes. Pug draws a knife. Chert raises her bat. Kellestine twirls his tire iron. He tells them they will not see the shine tomorrow. The thugs exchange uncertain glances, not understanding what that means, but they do not back off.
Kellestine charges first, tire iron swinging at the knife-wielder. Pug charges the pipe man. Chert moves in behind, bat up, trying to read the swing.
The pipe man lunges forward, overhead swing. Pug sidesteps, grabs him, uses his momentum to spin behind him. Pug drags his knife across the man’s throat. He collapses, clutching at his neck, gurgling on the ground.
Kellestine’s tire iron connects with the knife-wielder’s ribs. Bone cracks. The thug staggers, glaring, readying his knife. Chert’s baseball bat cracks into the back of his head. He drops to the floor.
The two thugs lie dying. One clutches at his throat. The other, barely conscious, blood dripping from the back of his head, tries to crawl away.
Footsteps from behind. Rapidly approaching. The three of them turn. Burr appears, having caught up. He runs past them without a word and stomps on the crawling thug, finishing him off.
Chert and Kellestine are stunned. Kellestine processes it. Bossman did not want the girl to become a murderer. He nods, as if ancient wisdom has just been passed down to him. Chert looks concerned, as if she does not quite buy it.
They redistribute the crates and the prisoner, moving more efficiently now. They make it back to the Community. Zero casualties on the first mission. The guards open the gate.

Snapshot
Summary
The group filters back into the guardhouse. Kitchen members take the supplies. A guard gestures them toward the debriefing room. Dux looks over the prisoner, up and down. The man is alive. Dux asks about the Death’s Head showing up.
He confirms the prisoner is not Death’s Head. No leathers. Death’s Head is the Syndicate that controls that territory. They have been coercing normal citizens into doing their dirty work. Dux had heard about it but did not think it was this bad. If the Death’s Head was not there before but has come back, this may be a good time for a show of force.
Get prepared. Dux will speak with Ben. Rest up. Take what you need. They march in half an hour.
The four of them rest. Dux returns with a displeased look. Ben says it is too risky. They should not engage. Dux shakes his head. Ben does not hold that authority. He is just a trusted advisor. Dux does not have to listen to advice that is not for the good of his people.
Dux and three other guards finish gearing up. They march after Burr. Kellestine is excited at the prospect of another fight. Chert appears uncertain, as if she thought it was only supposed to be one mission. Burr orders Kellestine to guard her. Kellestine nods and gives an imitation of a salute. Chert nods in thankfulness for the out.
Six of them head back to the warehouse district. No resistance along the way. Occasionally, shady figures glance at them from the alleys, but slink back upon eye contact.

Snapshot
Summary
The warehouse district comes into view. The Death’s Head see them approaching and begin yelling at each other. Men run out of the warehouse to line up, forming a wall of bodies. Both groups stand about thirty meters apart.
Dux yells to rally his men. They are here to reclaim what is theirs. To protect their people. His men yell back in affirmation. Dux charges. The Death’s Head holds for a moment, then breaks to meet them.
Dux clashes with an armored biker, his crowbar crashing against a tire iron and onto a shoulder. Burr charges in with a knife, feigning recklessness. A Death’s Head man with a tire iron prepares to meet him. The kick clips his arm. One breaks from the lines, trying to flank a guard. Burr circles behind him, grabs him, and stabs several times into his back, targeting the kidneys. The man collapses.
Another thug charges Burr, swinging a ratchet wrench. Before Burr can fully recover, another tries to kick at his knee. Burr sidesteps, ripping into the man’s groin with the claw end of his hammer. The man crumples. An armored biker charges Pug. Pug feints with one knife and stabs up into his throat with the other. Blood sprays across Pug’s face.
Burr sees a thug trying to tackle him. He twists, the claw edge of his hammer slamming into the man’s eye. He kicks the back of the man’s knee, hooks his head back, and snaps his neck.
The Death’s Head collectively decides the battle is lost. Fall back. Men retreat. The Community does not give chase immediately.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-03/day-03-su.title: Day 03 Summary
logs/pugburr/encounters/day-03/day-03-su.content:
Day 03 Summary

District 12, Post-Collapse — In-World Day 3
Agents: Pug (Welfare Department), Burr (Disciplinary Department)


Verified Lethals





































































#TargetCause of DeathEquipmentNotesEncounter1Death’s Head Warehouse Guard JerryRusted knife to throat—One of the armed warehouse occupants; charged Pug after the kitchen knife throw missed. Pug used a rusted knife that broke at the tang.3-2A2Shifty Pipe-wielding Road ThugKnife to throat—Ambushed the group on the road back to the Community demanding supplies3-2C3Shady Knife-wielding Road ThugStomped while crawling—Incapacitated by Kellestine and Chert, finished by Burr3-2C4Battered Death’s Head Armored BikerKnife to throat (feint)—Engaged Pug during the second battle. Pug feinted with one knife, stabbed into his throat with the other.3-3B5Kidney-knifed Death’s Head ThugMultiple stab wounds to back—Broke from the Death’s Head lines and was circled from behind by Burr during the Clash3-3B6Groin-clawed Death’s Head ThugClaw hammer to groin, pelvis fracture—Charged Burr, was met with the claw end of the hammer3-3B7Necksnapped Death’s Head ThugClaw to eye, neck snap—Tried to tackle charge Burr during the Clash; Burr reacted in time3-3B
Key Events

Morning community breakfast: mystery soup and stale water. Community supports over 100 people.
Guardhouse meetup with Dux at the armory. Met Chert (one-eyed woman with makeshift vest) and Kellestine (bald man in tank top).
Recovered confiscated weapons from shoebox: Burr’s knife, Pug’s knife, Burr’s brass knuckles.
Pug took 3 rusted knives and a butter knife from the armory rack.
Burr swapped boots for sandals, gave his stab-proof vest to Pug.
Chert and Kellestine assigned to join them. Burr refused. Two teams heading to same location.
3-1B: En Route. Travel to the warehouse district. Kellestine and Burr clash and bond over baldness and being killers. Chert shares her story with Pug. Warehouse district sighted ahead.
3-2A: The Warehouse Assault. Burr charges in, beats two occupants with brass knuckles. Pug engages a pipe-wielding thug in the second warehouse, kills him with a rusted knife that broke at the tang. Kitchen knife retrieved from floor. Prisoner taken, supplies looted (chicken broth, green beans, peaches, green peas). Kellestine kills one intruder, shaken by the experience.
3-2B: The Death’s Head. Reconnaissance phase. A dozen armed Death’s Head members arrive at the warehouse district. Burr evades without pursuit.
3-2C: The Road Ambush. Two thugs intercept the group on return. Pug kills Shifty Pipe-wielding Road Thug (knife to throat). Kellestine and Chert incapacitate the other; Burr finishes Shady Knife-wielding Road Thug by stomping. Zero Community casualties.
3-3A: Debrief and Return March. Dux interrogates the prisoner, learns Death’s Head use coerced civilians. Dux overrules Ben’s objection and leads a second march to the warehouse district with three guards. Burr grabs a claw hammer from the armory. Kellestine excited, Chert uncertain but given an out.
3-3B: Clash with the Death’s Head. Dux leads a charge. Burr kills three Death’s Head thugs (knife to kidneys, claw hammer to groin, claw to eye with neck snap). Pug kills a masked biker with a knife feint. Burr’s forearm bruised by ratchet wrench. Death’s Head retreats.
3-3C: Bloodied Pursuit. Pug fights two armored bikers. One takes a knife through the palm and flees (rusted knife lost). Pug disoriented from head impact and winded from solar plexus strike. Burr throws his claw hammer at civilian shields and loses it. Community forces withdraw. Death’s Head suffers many losses.
3-3D: A Quiet Discovery. Pug explores after treatment, finds a smuggling hole in the outer wall where a civilian retrieves cash from outside. Investigates but cannot reach the bills stored outside. Heads to Building B.
3-3E: Ben’s Intelligence. Ben shares Death’s Head history. Promises to interview the prisoner. Returns Pug’s E.G.O. handgun (6/7). Keep hidden, do not use within walls. Pug sees Chert working in the kitchen at dinner. Falls asleep.

Summary
A knock at the door. Pug opens it to find the same young boy from the stairway before. The doctors sent him to fetch Pug. Burr is waking up soon. He nods and runs off before Pug can respond.
Pug heads downstairs and crosses to the medical tents, but finds them empty. Too early for setup. He walks to Building B instead. Near the entrance, a small help desk points him to the right room. Down the hallway, last door on the right.
Opening the door, a doctor is already there. Right on time. He leads Pug inside. The room is a repurposed apartment, now a deeper medical wing. The tents outside are for field dressings; the intensive care cases are housed here. Burr lies in a bed, wounds dressed, a fresh bandage around his head. He slowly begins to stir.
Burr wakes, eyes bleary, double vision slowly clearing. He sees Pug’s face. Without a word, he tries to slide out of bed. His head aches, legs unsteady, balance failing. Pug catches him before his concussion meets the floor again.
The doctor clears his throat. He has good news and bad news. He hands over a small pill bottle. The good news is Burr can stand. The bad news is his brain is bleeding. Nothing they can do about it here, but these pills will keep the swelling down for now. If he rests, maybe a week to recover. If he does not, three or four days.
The doctor turns to Pug. There is a clinic nearby that should have HP pills in stock. Good chance it has not been looted yet. The Community needs supplies too. Perhaps they can help each other out. If Pug wants to save his friend, that is the option. When they get the Helapoeisis, bring it back here so the doctors can prepare it properly.
Burr is already walking away. Pug catches up.

Summary
They take the longer, more dangerous route. Open roads, exposed. After a few minutes of walking, four individuals in similar scavenger clothing eye them up and down. Hands resting on weapons that cannot be put away. But they make no move to accost the two of them. Continuing onward, the group relaxes again, keeping an eye on them but not following.
Twenty more minutes pass. Burr hears it first, his hyperaware state picking up on a single set of footsteps stepping out of an alley behind them. A man in ratty scavenger clothing, a face mask, wielding a metal pipe. He waves and yells something in the local language. The man does not understand them either. After some exchanged gestures, he nods and begins following along with them.
The path continues. The buildings begin to look less damaged, fewer shattered windows and broken doors. A man steps out of a building holding a small briefcase. He does not notice them until he closes the door.
The scavenger yells and moves forward past them, aiming his pipe threateningly. The man drops his briefcase and presses himself against the closed door, surprised. He asks what they want from him.
Coming up behind the scavenger who had placed his trust in them, Burr snaps his neck. The body drops to the floor. The briefcase man looks fearful and immensely confused. He gives them directions down the street and a right after two intersections. They are still on the right path. He picks up his briefcase and backs away, then turns and runs.

They eye the two agents warily. The agents mention the Community attack. One guard mutters that someone will get swept up. The other breaks into a coughing fit before dismissing it as not their problem. He tries to shoo them away with a wrench in his hand. Unless they are paying the toll.

The remaining guard drops the toll. Just pay 200 each. Then under his breath, a muttered curse. He opens his own wallet, tosses some bills into a small bucket, and waves them through. The information is worth more than the toll could ever be. He watches them pass, still standing guard.

Summary
Deeper into Death’s Head territory. Normal people walk the streets, though the area is sparse. The civilians share a common look: emaciated, pale, sunken eyes and gaunt cheeks. They avoid the two agents. Patrols are occasional, some members not even wearing leather vests.
The clinic comes into view ahead. The door opens. To their surprise, the shelves still hold medication, even if they could not be called full. The fluorescent lights flicker but stay on.
A tired man behind a counter waves them in. He gives a small, dry laugh. Someone dying? They have HP pills. Most were requisitioned by the Death’s Head for their war, but some remain. He reaches beneath the counter and produces a small foil sheet. Four 50mg Helapoeisis G9. Eighty thousand.
They cannot afford it. They offer the unmarked orange container of pills they have. He has no idea what that is. They can afford these mystery pills but not the HP pills?
They mention Koller. His eyes widen. They have had contact with Koller? They know where he is? If they tell him the location, he will deliver the HP pills himself. Just wait right here. He leaves through a door in the back.
Burr runs. Without hesitation, he bolts out of the store. Pug stays.
Running down a street, Burr sees five Death’s Head members approaching. Three pseudo-armored with thick pants and kneepads. Two armored bikers. The clinic their obvious goal. Burr tears off his disguise and tries to misdirect them. They ignore him, crossing the street toward the clinic.
Pug watches from inside the cafe across the street. Through the window, the Death’s Head members enter the clinic. The clerk pulls a screen and shows them something. The armored man turns and looks directly at the cafe.
Pug bolts. Through the kitchen, past confused workers. Two doors at opposite ends. He takes the left one and finds a back alley. He runs through the twisting alleyways, trying not to double back.
After catching his breath, the armored biker rounds a corner. The same one who locked eyes through the window. He wants to talk about a certain man.
The biker charges. Pug sidesteps and draws his knife. The man pivots, striking the knife aside with a bracer. A punch follows, ducked. They circle each other. Pug lunges, the blade glancing off the man’s ribs. The biker feints a punch and kicks at Pug’s side instead. Pug reads it, pushing back against the kick to reduce momentum. The kick still connects hard. Pug grabs the man’s leg, stabbing down into his achilles tendon. The man groans but tries to kick with his other foot. Pug twists the leg and throws it off. The man loses his footing, crashing into a trash can. Stunned. Unable to pursue.
Pug disengages, running deeper into the alley maze.
Meanwhile, Burr runs through his own maze of alleys. An hour passes before he finds an exit. The area looks different. Orange strips of fabric wrapped around lightposts. Death’s Head symbols crossed out by orange tally marks. He does not like what he sees. He returns into the alley.
Another hour passes. Eventually, another exit. Fewer Death’s Head patrols. More civilians. The buildings are larger, hardly any damage. A building catches his eye, odd in shape and standing out. The Time Machine.
Pug finds an exit of his own. By a miracle of the maze, he steps out into the same street. Burr is already there, staring at the strange wooden building.

Summary
The double doors swing open easily. What lies inside is a tragedy. A ruined bookstore. What must have once been a warm and comforting space, with twinkling lanterns on a chandelier, is now a dark room spanning the whole ground floor. Bookcases and shelves toppled. Books spilled and yanked to the floor. The Time Machine’s method of returning to the past was through the collection of books.
Burr scans around, then starts pulling and yanking books aside, adding to the mess. Pug peruses more carefully. Signs of battle are everywhere: blood splatters on dropped pages, destroyed furniture, slashes across wooden pillars. The maze of shelves continues deeper.
A red book catches Pug’s eye. Back to the Future. Pulling on its top triggers a mechanism. A bookcase near the back creaks. Burr pulls it open. A secret tunnel.
Inside, wood paneling lines the walls. Portraits hang alongside synthetic potted plants. At the end of the hallway, an elevator door with a small end table next to it. A bowl of five red apples.
Burr takes two out. Puts them back. Pug pushes the elevator button. It lights up. The mechanism whirs to life. Burr takes one apple. Pug takes one. Three remain.
The doors open to reveal a shabby lift. Like something from a mineshaft. Rusting metal frame, crumbling brick surround, a grate floor showing pure blackness below. A single lever instead of buttons.
They step inside. The doors close on their own. Nothing happens. Burr pulls the lever. The lift jostles and begins descending, scraping against the wall. Sparks fly. Small pieces of brick crumble down on them.
It stops. Stuck.
Pug braces himself. Oh no. Burr jumps. The lift dislodges and descends into near free-fall. They drop to the floor. Sparks fly everywhere as the emergency brakes catch near the end of the chain. The momentum passes through them. The lift slows, then stops.
Ding. The doors open.

Summary
The elevator doors open halfway covered by the floor. Burr climbs out, his torso caught between elevator and floor level. The elevator begins to lift back upward. It stops at floor level. They step out into a large workshop.
Dim lights. Flickering. Their eyes are drawn to the ceiling. Dozens, approaching a hundred, prosthetic and cybernetic arms hang like ornaments. Around the room: workshop stations, a surgery area, a reclining chair surrounded by cables and monitors. A living area with a low couch and two beanbag chairs in front of a flatscreen TV. An electronics corner with half a dozen monitors, keyboards, tablets, and phones connected by DIY wiring.
Burr spots a small door in the wall. He opens it.
A familiar face stares back. The scientist man from before, pants half pulled down, sitting on a toilet with a bowl of ice cream and a spoon. He blinks a couple of times. Is cizinec here on appointment? He hands them the bowl and spoon. Please take this while I get ready.
The door closes. A flush. He walks out, putting on fresh prosthetic hands from a plastic bag.
They explain about Burr’s brain bleed. Koller nods. He looks like he is dying. The easiest option is Helapoeisis. Hardest would be a bolus, but he is not from H corp. He does not know what goes into them. Mutations and such. Finding a good supplier would be basically impossible.
He cannot put any parts in them for free. The only thing he can offer for free is a proper diagnosis. A brain scan.
He sets up the machine. A ring attached to a multi-jointed servomechanical arm lowered onto Burr’s head. Wires with frayed ends taped on. The monitors show an update screen. It needs to update first.
While they wait, Koller tosses Pug a lighter. Pug takes a hit.
The machine finishes updating. Koller runs the scan. The arm moves, the ring spinning one way then the other. Koller goes to sit in a beanbag chair.
The atmosphere is tense. Koller notices. Pug is asked if he is dying too. They discuss fallen feathers. Both of them. Koller’s eyes widen. Both of them are fallen feathers? You guys sure are everywhere.
The scan finishes. He heads to the monitors. Some damage, but the medicine seems to be doing its job. The machine has been on the fritz lately. He cannot see any bleeding. Either the machine is breaking, or Burr has a healthy brain for a dying man.
Koller offers to order supplies. SuperEats can deliver to the Community. They need to give him an address and a description of the man who will receive it. Devyat may kill the delivery man if he takes an order without authorization. They give Ben’s description.
He gestures to the couch. It is a pull-out. A small first-aid sized pouch contains a blanket and pillow. Pug reaches inside. His arm is swallowed by the darkness. He finds them.
They smoke and relax, waiting for night to come. Koller sits criss-cross in his chair, playing games on his computer. Let me know when the client is here.

Summary
A couple of hours pass. The elevator begins to screech and half-crash again. Koller yells from his computer. Let them in. He cannot pause.
The doors open. A young woman climbs out. White hair, mismatched gray and blue eyes. A skirt worn over leggings, a thick jacket, a thin black cloak reaching the middle of her back with the hood pulled back. A spear in one hand, a sheathed machete on her hip. She pulls down a respirator and breathes normally.
She ignores Pug. Are you his assistant? She strolls past, brushing by without waiting for an answer. She stands in the middle of the room, scanning her surroundings. Her eyes land on the bong with disdain. She waits for Koller to finish his game.
She notices the hot pocket on the plate. She takes the unbitten one and replaces it with a red apple. She stares at Burr, as if waiting to see if he will tattle. Her stoic poker face shifts to a disappointed look. Have you had these apples? Go and try them. She will not spoil the fun. Suit yourself. She eats the hot pocket silently.
Cheese. Some kind of meat. It is good.
She pushes the plate with Koller’s bitten hot pocket toward them. Biting into the red apple, it is chalky and crumbly. Definitely an apple. The worst one they have had. At least someone will eat them.
Koller finishes his game. His face falls at the sight of his last hot pocket being eaten. His eye twitches. The woman brought a package. Some bumps in the road, but the package is unharmed. He gives her a package of green vials in return. Two weeks worth.
She turns to leave. Stops in front of both agents. You look like you are dying. She scans their faces, dismisses a thought. Hope you get better.
She steps into the elevator. A small wave. Hope you hatchlings find what you are looking for.
The door closes.
They settle for the night. Koller sleeps in his chair, an eyemask over his eyes, headphones on. The faint sound of ASMR plays through them.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-04/day-04-su.content:
Day 04 Summary

District 12, Post-Collapse - In-World Day 4
Agents: Pug (Welfare Department), Burr (Disciplinary Department)


Verified Lethals





















#TargetCause of DeathEquipmentNotesEncounter1Trusting Pipe-wielding ScavengerNeck snapMetal pipeFollowed the agents through Death’s Head territory then threatened a civilian with a briefcase. Burr killed him from behind during the confusion.4-2A
Key Events

Morning: Pug visits Burr in Building B medical wing. Doctor diagnoses brain bleed, gives anti-swelling pills. Directs them to a clinic in Death’s Head territory for HP pills.
Meeting with Dux at Ben’s office. Directions to Koller’s office deep in Death’s Head territory. Disguises taken from the closet.
Travel through Death’s Head territory. Four scavengers eye them but don’t attack. An alley scavenger follows and joins them, then threatens a civilian. Burr snaps his neck.
Death’s Head checkpoint. Agents bluff about the Community attack, one guard runs to warn others. The remaining guard waves them through.
Clinic visit. Clerk has HP pills for 80,000 but won’t accept unmarked pills. Mentions Koller, leaves to “sort something out.” Burr runs. Pug stays.
Death’s Head members arrive at the clinic, shown camera footage. Pug escapes through a cafe kitchen. Burr tears off his disguise and misdirects.
Pug fights an armored biker in the alleys, cuts his achilles and escapes.
Burr wanders the alley maze for over an hour, finds orange-flagged territory with crossed-out Death’s Head symbols. Returns to the maze.
Both agents find The Time Machine by different paths. Enter the ruined bookstore, discover the secret tunnel.
Elevator descent into Koller’s workshop. Harrowing free-fall ride.
Meeting Koller, brain scan, discussion of treatment options and fallen feathers. Lighter obtained.
The client arrives. Young woman with white hair and mismatched eyes. Exchange of packages. Calls them “hatchlings” and leaves.
Night falls. They sleep at Koller’s workshop.

Summary
A blaring alarm rips through the workshop. The screens flash red. A light fixture on the front spins red, jolting both agents awake. Koller continues dozing, snoring peacefully in his chair.
Pug finds a digital clock: 04:24. Koller sniffs in his sleep and jolts awake, pulling up his sleep mask and headphones. He mutters in confusion, then turns on his desktop. An update screen pops up. He throws his arms up in exasperation — his joke ruined. He presses a different button and shuts off the alarm. Ten minutes before something was scheduled, but the last wave should already be done sweeping. Nothing to worry about.
Before leaving, Pug returns Koller’s lighter. Koller waves them off. The two agents head up the elevator and out through the secret tunnel, emerging at the front of The Time Machine. The street is empty, the morning still dark, streetlights still on.
Making their way into the alley system and trying to retrace their steps, they take a left and attempt a right turn. The slim alleyway has been blocked off by a sheet metal barricade. A different path, previously blocked, now has no obstacles. Pug slams into the barricade — a few layers give way and bend before striking a metal wall that is even stronger. The full force of his tackle reverberates. Part of the sheet metal is the corrugated wall of a shipping container.

One man with a shortsword, wearing a blazer, loosening his tie. The other, a large tanned man, tattoos spanning up and down his arms, chain necklaces and rings on both hands.
The tattooed man sees them and bellows. He demands they stop and watch. The swordsman charges from behind, seeking to pierce his heart. The tattooed man spins, his right arm’s tattoos glowing as his fist barrels toward the swordsman’s face. The air ripples from the impact. The man flies backward, crashing into the wall with a bloody stain.
The tattooed man turns his attention to the agents.
They run. He chases. His stride is longer than it should be — boosted. Burr dropkicks the air, an improvised feint. The tattooed man swats him aside. Burr crashes through a window, his pelvis slamming the wall. He lands inside the building, dazed, a throbbing pain in his hip.
The tattooed man catches Pug by the jacket. Special move, rat! Throw! He yanks and pivots, hurling Pug into a pile of garbage bags against a dumpster. Back slams against metal.
The Stray Dogs member walks off. Waste of fucking time.

Summary
Taking another route, the agents continue to hobble down the alleys, lost, with vultures on their trail. Footsteps of scavengers approach from behind, biding their time, growing impatient.
They stumble into a clearing. A group of five men ahead. Leather vests, road goggles, motorcycle helmets. Death’s Head. They crouch around a body on the floor. They see the agents hobbling closer.
One steps forward. Hey! What happened? Their stoic faces go pale when they hear the answer. Stray Dogs.
The scavengers close in from behind. Surrounded. Two routes out of the alley, both blocked.
A sixth man rounds the corner behind the Death’s Head. An armored biker, complete set of kneepads, elbowpads, gloves, a full-face helmet, a full leather jacket instead of a vest. On his shoulder, a fireaxe dripping with blood. He is splattered with it. He breathes heavily beneath his helmet.
Get on the ground. Spread your hands out.
The sixth man walks forward, undeterred. His steps make no noise. He walks right behind the back three men. He pivots, twists, crouches. The axe cleaves through five ankles. Cuts halfway through the sixth.
The men scream. Chaos. A tire iron cracks against his side. He barely flinches. He kicks the leader in the chest, then swings the axe like a baseball bat into his ribcage. He uses the embedded axe to swing the man around, crashing him into the second standing man.
The agents limp away as fast as they can. Help! Use your gun! They round a corner. One last glimpse: the axe-man has walked toward the remaining man. He pulls back his glove. Drives it forward. The air whirs. The screaming stops.
They continue limping. Two hours later, they reach the alley that connects to the cafe.

The two agents finally reach the alleyway, stopping to catch their breaths. The backdoor of the shop is closed, but at least it is familiar. Opening the door into the cafe kitchen — empty. Heading through to the customer area: the restaurant is completely empty. A sign on the glass door says OPEN. Yellow tape spread across the entrance.
Through the windows, they spot two individuals across the street. One in a dirty white dress shirt, sleeves rolled up, a crooked green necktie. A sword strapped to his hip. The other in a neater but frayed green suit jacket, bespectacled, dirty white gloves, holding a clipboard. A shortsword in a leather ring holster. They inspect the clinic — also yellow-taped.
Pug heads out through the side door to the street. The bespectacled man hails him. He confirms the clinic is closed. Best of luck.
Burr hobbles past the checkpoint. Three Death’s Head members — two thugs and one biker — are too focused on their conversation about the axe-man to stop him. They gossip about being posted there after what happened to their allies. Burr passes through without issue.
One intersection, then another. Eventually, Burr finds himself in front of the timid man’s apartment building. The one whose life they saved. No trace of the scavenger’s body remains.

Summary
Burr knocks on the door. Time passes. He knocks again. No response. He tries the handle — the door opens without effort. The locking mechanism is not broken.
Inside, a hallway. A small shelf near a desk filled with lockboxes. A staircase leading up. Doors line the hallway.
He knocks on the third door on the left. No reply. He goes door to door. The sixth door on the left finally responds. A gruff voice asks what he wants. Described as every limp noodle-backed spineless fuck around here. Not interested. Go pick it up by the mailboxes and fuck off.
Back down to the lockboxes. All closed. No package in sight. A padlock on the floor, sliced cleanly in half. A lockbox with room number 105 underneath — no padlock. It opens easily. Inside, a small package in teal packaging, yellow ropes wrapped around and binding it. No knot in sight. A heavily stylized logo: the number 9 surrounded by a briefcase shaped like the letter D.
He brings the box to Room 105 — the third door on the left. No response. A shadow flickers in the peephole. The door creaks open. The timid man is confused. Some mailman knocked, said he would cut it down in ten seconds, made him sign a paper, put it in his lockbox. He did not even give the mailman his key.
Burr asks for something to carry it in. The timid man returns with a shoebox. He is confused — Burr is just giving it to him? Not coming back to demand a favor? Right. Thanks.
Burr tries to pry the yellow rope off. It shimmers when tugged. Does not budge.
He leaves the apartment building. The door closes behind him.

Burr hobbles back to the checkpoint. The biker is gone. Two thugs remain. One stands up from leaning on a wall. Saw you leave earlier. You know the drill. Does not have to be harder than it has to be. He holds out a hand. You pay coming in. No exceptions.
Burr argues. Mentions the axe-man. The thugs grow suspicious and agitated. They are not willing to listen anymore. Weapons drawn, but not attacking. The option to walk away remains.
Burr sets the box aside. Are you fucking crazy? You got a deathwish?
The fight begins. The thugs back up through the checkpoint, poised to strike through the chokepoint. Burr glides forward, jabbing. The first man evades cautiously. The second strikes Burr’s left shoulder from behind — painful, but not fully committed.
Burr pivots, elbowing the first man in the jaw. He stumbles. The second man strikes at Burr’s leg, trying to trip him up. Burr spins into a straight kick, catching the man in the chin. He stumbles backward onto the floor, head spinning.
Burr turns to the first man, pressing the advantage. A right cross is blocked. A front kick is caught. Burr jumps, twisting into a kick to the side of the man’s head. He blocks, stumbling back. Burr breaks his fall, pushes himself forward, and kicks the man in the nose. He tumbles backward, his pipe clattering away.
Both men groan on the floor, defeated.
Burr picks up the box and leaves. Pug follows. Passing through the checkpoint, they return to the cafe. The two green-suited men have finished at the clinic. They walk past. The bespectacled one raises an eyebrow. Good to see you got your package.

Summary
Retracing their steps with heightened senses and memory, they move hastily. Spotting potential threats before they take note, understanding when to back off and reroute, when to hide and let pass. It takes a fraction of the time — a better route devised through growing familiarity. Just barely under an hour to return to The Time Machine.
The elevator rides smoothly, no catching or hitching this time.
Stepping out into the workshop, they are greeted by the sight of Koller on the floor, face down. He lets out a large sigh, then quickly jumps to attention, flipping over and righting himself into a sitting position. Oh it is you two pritel! You are back? Already? He gazes at the package, then looks up at their state. Huh. You two get hit by truck on the way? This is way ahead of expectations, good job pritel! He pauses, then pales. What kind of tattoos?
Koller listens as they describe the Stray Dogs encounter. You two are lucky to be alive. Too many clients turned to ground beef by those dogs.
He takes the package graciously and heads to his computer. He has been doing research. Searching for easy jobs for new Fixers. Lost cat — pay seems OK. Bodyguard duty — many want it, few takers. A man wants volunteers to check abandoned structures. Something to do with the collapse. Koller advises against it — the man preys on greed. Small jobs, lay low, build up, stay alive.
Koller does not have much to give them. He can install augments for a fee. For weapons and gear — buy from shops or take from enemies. The treasure hunt starts the day after tomorrow. Always last minute.
Pug brings up the E.G.O. handgun. Koller recognizes it. He explains that he and many others were unable to crack one open. On close inspection it really should not work — and yet it does. No trace of manufacturing. One thing they figured out: the safety automatically engages when the last round is chambered, preventing the user from firing the final bullet without manually toggling the safety off.
Koller tries to reach a former client who stole ink from the Stray Dogs. He sends a message. Two hours pass. A client comes in and delivers a package to Koller. No message back from the former client.
They wait a couple more hours. Koller plays games, works on prosthetics, does research. The clock hits 8 PM. No message from the former client.
Pug shows Koller the key details about his prosthetic situation. Koller asks them not to make staying over a habit. Night falls in the Backstreets.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-05/day-05-su.content:
Day 05 Summary

District 12, Post-Collapse — In-World Day 5
Agents: Pug (Welfare Department), Burr (Disciplinary Department)


Verified Lethals











#TargetCause of DeathEquipmentNotesEncounter
(No kills by agents on Day 5)
Key Events

04:24 AM alarm at Koller’s workshop. Brief false alert, Koller shuts it down. Pug returns Koller’s lighter. Agents depart at dawn.
Alley paths shifted overnight — previous route blocked by shipping container barricade, new path opened.
Stray Dogs encounter: a tattooed Syndicate member fights a man with a shortsword, kills him with a single powered punch. Chases Pug and Burr. Burr flung through a window (hip injury). Pug thrown into a dumpster (back injury). The Stray Dogs member leaves them bruised but alive.
Alley scavengers track them from rooftops like vultures. The sword-man’s body dragged into a building.
Cornered by five Death’s Head members and scavengers. A sixth armored biker with a fireaxe arrives — cleaves five ankles, kills three Death’s Head members with brutal efficiency. Agents limp away as he finishes the survivors. Two-hour limp back to the cafe alley.
Cafe is closed, yellow-taped. Two men in green suits (swords on hips) inspecting the closed clinic across the street. One hails Pug; confirms the clinic is closed.
Burr passes through a checkpoint. Death’s Head members too focused on gossip about the Stray Dogs to stop him.
Burr reaches the timid man’s apartment building. Door unlocked. Finds a Devyat Association package (logo: 9 inside a D-shaped briefcase) in lockbox 105. The timid man provides a shoebox. Yellow ropes on the package shimmer and resist prying.
Checkpoint fight: Burr fights two Death’s Head thugs to pass back through. Wins despite injuries. Picks up the box and walks through with Pug following.
Agents return to The Time Machine in under an hour. Elevator works smoothly.
Koller receives the package. Discusses the Stray Dogs — calls them bad for business.
Koller searches for jobs: lost cat, bodyguard duty, a treasure-hunting expedition (day after tomorrow, something about the Collapse). Advises against the expedition.
Koller explains augment installation policy. Will install if they bring prosthetics. For gear: buy from shops or take from enemies.
Pug shows Koller the E.G.O. handgun. Koller explains it cannot be disassembled, no manufacturing marks, and the safety auto-engages on the last bullet.
Koller tries to contact a former client who stole Stray Dogs ink. No reply by 8 PM.
Agents go to bed. Koller asks them not to make staying over a habit.
Night falls.

Summary
The two agents awaken naturally. The clock reads 5 AM. Koller is still asleep in his chair. They get up, situate themselves, and head up the elevator. The ride is uneventful, and they emerge from The Time Machine into the pre-dawn streets.
Feeling better than yesterday, but by no means fully healed, they set out on main roads instead of the alleyways. The main streets are less dangerous this early in the morning, especially in the center of Death’s Head territory.
After about half an hour of walking, they near the clinic. A Death’s Head patrol of three men spots them: two thugs and one with reinforced pants and a face mask. Burr recognizes one of the thugs — an older man, the father of the young man he lifted and killed in the first warehouse raid.
The old man stops in the street, shocked. He recognizes Burr. He cannot forgive him. Not for his son. Not for the others he killed. He raises a small carpenter’s hammer, too small to be effective, but held faithfully. The other two raise their weapons. The biker steps forward.
Words fall on deaf ears. The three charge.
Burr meets them head-on. A knee to the biker’s face staggers him. A backstep evades the second man’s stool leg swing, then a liver blow drops him. The old man strikes Burr in the side with his hammer — the small head cracks against his ribs. Pug dropkicks the old man in the chest, knocking him down and sending the hammer clattering. Burr finishes with the biker, two knuckles to the solar plexus.
All three are down, alive. Burr checks pulses. The old man is wheezing but breathing. Burr moves them into recovery positions. They walk off.

Taking the main streets, they approach the checkpoint area. A Death’s Head thug is visible ahead, leaning back in a chair in the shade. The breeze carries a metallic scent — blood.
Rounding the corner, they find a headless man in the chair. A large wound in the middle of his chest. Past the checkpoint, two more bodies lie in various pieces and states of hewed disassembly. The axe-man’s work.
Pug and Burr rifle through pockets. Wallets, all empty of cash. Blood stains their hands from the wallets. The toll bucket has been cleaned out. Searching for weapons, they find a bent tire iron, a broken wrench, and a pool cue snapped in half. Particles of glass and grey-black plastic litter the scene.
Bloody footprints lead into an alleyway. They follow. The path twists, ending at a dumpster. Multiple footprints surround it. Burr opens the lid — a motorcycle helmet stares back. Nestled atop bloody clothes. No person within.
Burr retrieves the helmet, a leather vest, thick denim pants, and bloody boots. No kneepads, elbowpads, or jacket. The air inside the helmet smells of sweat and blood, with a sharp, cold scent mixed in — familiar from the cafe.
Burr puts on the grimy, blood-soaked gear. Much of it still wet, smearing as he wears it. Pug watches from a distance, keeping watch.
They head back towards the cafe, passing the checkpoint crime scene without paying any toll.

Returning to the cafe, the yellow tape is gone, but the store remains closed. Burr tracks bloody footprints inside.
They head to the kitchen. The smell from the helmet is not from here — it was stronger at the front of the store. Going behind the counter, Burr removes the helmet. The front of the store absolutely emanates the same sharp, cold note present in the helmet. He hands it to Pug. The scent is prominent with sweat and blood, with an intermingled third scent — coffee. But the cafe itself lacks the sharp coldness. The scent is similar but not the same.
With nothing else to investigate, Burr raids the kitchen. He finds vacuum-sealed pouches marked with a B. Two tins — one of oats, one of granola. Pug opens a pouch — a condensed brown mass expands rapidly into a loaf of bread. He tears into it, scoffing it down.
Burr searches for cutlery. Most has been taken out. But he finds a bread cutting knife and takes it.
They leave the cafe and head back towards the checkpoint, passing through without issue. The Community awaits.

The rest of the journey is similar — scavengers and thugs eye them warily from a distance.
At the Community gate, guards yell down. Hey! You two! Stop! State your business! They recognize Pug but not the Death’s Head uniform. Burr lifts his visor to show his hair. The guards let them in. A search is required — safety protocol.
The guards search Burr. They take the Death’s Head gear for secure storage in the armory lockers. The bread knife goes with it. They gesture to Burr to spread his arms.
The guards update them on events: the prisoner was found dead in his cell. Suicide. Ben accuses Dux. Dux claims he is innocent. Dux is holed up in Building C, awaiting trial. He does not trust anyone.
Burr heads to the armory to deposit the gear. The quartermaster jokes with him. No walking around in Death’s Head gear inside the walls. It would cause panic.
