Summary
Pug and Burr approach the spider room. The hallway is quiet. A single spider crawls across the floor, baseball-sized, with one bulbous body section, a pincer mouth, and six legs. It ignores them completely. They walk around it and continue onward. At the end of the hallway, dozens upon dozens of the creatures cover the floor, walls, and ceiling. The floor is thick with them. Neither the skull mace nor the spiders react to each other.
Burr points at a spider and yells for it to die. It does nothing. One drops onto Pug’s head. He brushes it off.
Burr runs. He crushes a spider underfoot. Every eye in the hallway lights up, glowing red. The swarm turns and charges. Spiders launch themselves from the walls and ceiling, latching onto Burr’s body as he runs. They bite into his flesh, tearing small chunks from his body, their paralytic agent spreading through his limbs. More pour from the room, climbing over each other, three to four deep, rushing toward him. Pug aims the lever-action rifle and squeezes the trigger. Nothing happens.
Burr bursts into the room. Cocoons hang from the ceiling. No large spider in sight. Whatever spun the hanging body from the camera feed was something else entirely.
Pug strips down mid-fight, pulling off his corporate suit to don the dark funeral suit from the lockers. Burr dives into the swarm, scrounging on the floor as the spiders tear into him. His mangled hand clasps around bloodstained bills. He surfaces, barely holding on, and pushes past Pug.
Nozzles extend from the ceiling and begin spraying a blue-tinted gas. The air takes on a sweet, acidic smell. The spiders slow. The agents limp through the hallway, leaving a trail of blood.
At the vending machine, Burr drinks a red soda. His flesh knits together. A blue soda clears the toxins. A purple soda restores his ring finger, his eyelid, most of his cheek. A permanent scar remains. The wounds are still open and painful, but no longer bleeding profusely. He finds himself able to walk.

Summary
The group returns to Sir Tatum looking drastically different from when they departed. Pug is clad in the dark funeral suit — a two-piece set of choking black with pointed shoes and black leather gloves, the lever-action rifle in hand and the small cane with a black fedora tucked at his side. Burr is a bloody, tattered mess — his body still bearing the marks of the spider swarm, chunks of flesh torn away and his outfit riddled with holes. The rest of the group stares in stunned silence at their transformed appearances.
Sir Tatum beams at the sight. “Most excellent work! I’ll be tallying this up.” Sean, the turtleneck man, is vocal about Pug and Burr’s exploits — recounting their actions in the armory, the spider room, and everything in between.
The client addresses the entire group directly. He instructs ALL adventurers to leave all outfits and items found during the expedition for appraisal. He will take down addresses for payment distribution once the appraisal is complete.
Burr reaches up and tugs at the noose around his neck. The knot loosens, and the dark funeral outfit — the one from Locker 3 — disappears into a neatly folded stack, still riddled with spider holes from the swarm. Beneath it, his old corporate suit is revealed, itself full of holes where the spiders had torn through. The client takes note of Burr’s clear preference for his original outfit, remarking that he will keep it in mind as a priority.
Pug likewise surrenders the items retrieved from Locker 3: the dark funeral suit, the lever-action rifle, and the small cane topped with the black fedora. He re-equips his old corporate suit — the charcoal grey wool with white dress shirt and red tie, torn and bloodied from prior fights — and retrieves his samurai armor from storage, donning it once more.
The group files into the elevator. The tension is palpable. Sean and his colleagues are not happy with how events have unfolded. The raincoat individual is similarly displeased. The fixers remain antsy, hands near their weapons. Only Sir Tatum seems genuinely cheerful, humming to himself as the doors close.
The elevator ride is tense and quiet. No one speaks.
During the descent, the raincoat individual slowly pulls out a small plastic pouch — an emergency water ration containing water mixed with various electrolytes. They offer it to Burr. He drinks a few sips — the water tastes like standard mineral water — then hands it to Pug, who also drinks some. The pouch cannot be resealed; whatever remains will go to waste.

Summary
The elevator doors slide open, and the group is met with utter carnage. Bodies litter the floor — many pulverized, crushed, or missing parts of themselves. The death did not happen all at once, nor in a single location; the carnage continues into the lobby room and all along the elevator hallway, a trail of destruction stretching outward from the building’s depths.
Sir Tatum steps out into the hallway. He lifts his cane, pressing a button — the bottom of it unfolds into an umbrella. Overhead, the sprinklers spray down onto the blood-soaked floor. The alarm lights, having gone quiet, blare a hellish red glow across the flesh-corrupted surroundings. He takes out a pocket watch with his right hand, glances at it, then looks back to those in the elevator. He gestures — a simple motion for everyone to lead the way.
Burr heads on first, moving into the carnage. The fixers and the raincoat individual begin heading toward the stairs, guiding the way out.
As they pass through the lobby, the extent of the devastation becomes clear. The floor guardian — the Janitor — lies among the wreckage. Its remains are gruesome: one arm sliced clean off, the other hacked to pieces, its head missing entirely. Broken blades and shaft fragments stick out from the mangled corpse. A large, cavernous hole gapes in its chest — the heart has been ripped out. The floor guardian is no longer a threat. Dead. Confirmed.
The climb up the stairs is uneventful. The group ascends past floors where the Flesh had climbed higher than before — reaching further than during the initial descent. They do not stop. They push upward until they reach the top floor, emerging into a barren office space.
Sir Tatum takes a moment to collect addresses for payment delivery. The raincoat individual stands apart, providing no information. Sir Tatum warns them about the contract — but does not stop them when they make no move to cooperate. The raincoat simply leaves, heading up the stairs. The door swings open, and swings shut behind them.
Pug and Burr linger. Sir Tatum mentions that his escort has orders to eliminate anyone else who remains in the building — they should not go back inside. Pug and Burr express their preferences for the appraised items — which pieces they would like to claim once evaluated. Sir Tatum listens carefully: “I am hearing your preferences, and shall take them into account. I shall pass the message along once the appraiser finishes their duties.” No promises, but acknowledgment.
Stepping outside, they find Sean’s crew resting. The fixers are arguing amongst themselves — one of their three members is still inside. Six individuals wait nearby: four with heavy batons, riot helmets, and padded armor; two in long navy coats — one carrying a longsword, the other a zweihander.
Sean approaches. “Good work back there… You’re surely getting the biggest cut of all of us.” He pauses. “Try not to get yourselves killed.” A beat. “Hopefully on the same side next time.”
The baton-wielding members draw their weapons and head into the building. Their work is not yet done.
Pug and Burr leave the ruins of the Fallen Wing behind, heading back the way they came. The encounter is over. The building — and everything within it — is behind them.

Clambering down from the walls, returning on the crushed and crumbled road, leaving the ruined buildings of the Fallen Wing behind. Lips parched and stomachs grumbling, Pug and Burr catch a scent on the air — something good. The smell leads them down a small side street to an unmarked building with a curtain draped over the entryway, like a small local restaurant. An older voice calls out: “Ah! More customer? You want food? Come in!”
As they begin to enter, they nearly walk into a man exiting. Tall, wearing sunglasses, a navy coat with brown lapels, black gloves, a brown vest over a light yellow dress shirt. Not a uniform, but styled as such. “Comin’ through~” he says, sidestepping past them and heading down the street.
Burr calls after him — asks if he works for the Zwei Association. The man, already some distance away, turns back. He takes one hand from his pocket, gives a wave and a cheeky grin. “I didn’t see any Zwei here, don’t think you did either.” He turns, hand back in pocket, and continues on his way.
Inside, the restaurant is small and cozy. An older woman behind the counter. A few tables and counter seats. One other customer remains — a woman in a grey sports sweatshirt and unmarked baseball cap, with short pale purple hair. A plate of grilled fish sits before her, with two glasses — one mostly full of water, the other half-empty with what looks like beer or ale.
She looks up as they enter, glances between them, and takes a sip of water. “The barbeque beef platter is good.” Her voice is low, silky.
The shopkeeper welcomes them warmly. Large platter is 1,000 Ahn, normal is 750. Water — tap or bottle. Pug orders for both of them. The shopkeeper returns with two plates balanced on one arm, a bottle of water, and two plastic cups pinched between her fingers. “OKOK! You two eat up! Look like shit! Need to eat more!”
The plates hold five thin pieces of beef with a distinct piece of fat on one end, a mound of rice, sliced cucumber and tomato, and a small bowl of thin light orange sauce. The total is 3,500 Ahn.
The beef is slightly rubbery, not quite tender, but very flavorful — pairing well with the sauce and rice. Filling and satisfying. As they eat, Burr grumbles about the cost, prompting a short suppressed exhale from behind. The woman in the cap remains motionless, composed.
Burr eventually confronts her — he knows who she is. She keeps a blank, almost bored stare, patting her mouth with a towelcloth. She tilts her head, not understanding. Then she reaches into her bag and pulls out a yellow raincoat. The confirmation is silent but clear: she is the raincoat individual from the Fallen Wing.
As Pug and Burr finally leave, passing through the curtain, they hear her softly speak: “You too.”

Summary
The two of them trek onwards, heading toward the workshop. Returning through Death’s Head territory, the border guard looks them up and down with an awkward expression. “Uh.. Yeah.. Your uh.. a lot is showing.” Burr deadpans: “Un…fortunate… ?” The guard stammers: “You tooo.. hope it gets better.”
Passing deeper into controlled territory, Death’s Head patrols notice them — and immediately steer clear. The reputation earned from the Pound breakout and Stray Dog fight precedes them.
Past the Community now, and continuing towards the workshop. Down the street, a scene unfolds: five Rat Thugs with weapons drawn surround an individual in a long silky grey coat. A silver monocle catches the light. Short white hair pulled back into a small ponytail. Two large leather satchels on their hips, each emblazoned with a fanciful cursive “R” logo — androgynous, difficult to read as male or female. Their arms are up in surrender, inching backward as the rats inch forward.
Burr acts first. He reaches past the nearest rat and snaps his neck before he can even yelp. Pug sweeps another, stabs down into him — dead in seconds.
Two more rats turn, shocked. Pug and Burr kick simultaneously — both knees snap backward at impossible angles. The rats howl and fall. The last one turns to run. Burr catches him, lifts him by the neck, squeezes until he goes limp. Pug kicks the knee-broken rat in the head — he cracks against the pavement and goes still. Burr, fury still hot, uses the unconscious rat to pummel the other knee-broken one into the street, over and over, until both are still.
The merchant stumbles backward, falling onto the sidewalk. “Wh — Huh? I can’t do that. I need them for the projects I’m working on. I do appreciate the assistance, would you take payment?”
Their name is Rune. A textile trader. They were “mid negotiating their price” with the rats — a claim they acknowledge sounds absurd from the agents’ perspective. They reach into their wallet — holding roughly 30,000,000 Ahn. Initial offer: 10,000 each. Haggling ensues.
Rune glances at a watch, winces. “What about 500,000?” Pause. They look again. “Ah… Could you do 400,000? In total.”
A deal. Rune hands over the stack. “Goodbye fellows! Please make sure to pay the tax on that!”
As Pug and Burr continue toward the workshop, they hear a small explosion in the distance behind them.

Summary
Pug and Burr eventually find themselves in front of a small, decrepit, looted storefront. Its sign has been taken down. The inside is dark, illuminated only by light through shattered windows. Glass shards crunch underfoot. Another one of many dilapidated buildings.
They search for a hatch or bunker door. Pug enters a back room, finds empty workshop tables. Backing into a corner to survey the room — he is standing directly on a metal hatch. Burr steps in, finds him there. Producing a key from the latchbox set, Burr inserts it into the hatch. A slow, methodical turn. The mechanisms click. The key turns fully — and snaps off. But the hatch is unlocked.
Lifting the heavy metal door with effort, they descend into pitch black. Burr’s flashlight flickers — nearly dead. A few shakes and smacks coax a faint glow. The light passes over blades without handles, small tools, machining tables. A lightswitch hangs from the ceiling — pulling it does nothing.
Burr backtracks and finds a generator. Cranking it, the engine roars to life. Fluorescent lights flicker on across the bunker.
The workshop is revealed. A large maul leans against the wall — rebar handle with rubberized grips, a car battery welded into place as the maul head, reinforced with steel. Extremely destructive but heavy and off-balance.
Nearby on a table: two daggers. One forged from a railroad spike — a curved blade with a brass knuckle grip. The other: thinner, lighter blade with a cylindrical handle, a button near the top, and a small mechanism at its base.
At the center of the workshop: two armor suits on racks. The first is heavy — an amalgamation of leather and sheet metal: a thick duster with layered metal plates, a welded metal helmet with an integrated welding mask, heavy construction gloves with metal knuckle protection, and rubberized metal-reinforced boots. Extremely protective but cumbersome. The second is lighter — a long leather duster with thin metal sewn into the fabric, tire rubber reinforcement, deep pockets throughout, and a leather hood reinforced with rubber and steel.
They gear up. Pug takes the light armor and the slim dagger. Burr dons the heavy armor set, taking the car battery maul and the railroad spike dagger. The armor is cumbersome — restricted movement, shuffling and clinking with every step. The heavy armor severely limits range of motion; the lighter set less so.
Equipped and ready, they haul themselves back to the surface, peering down one last time at the illuminated bunker before closing the hatch.

Summary
Heading back to the Community, completely armored up and ready for anything, they eventually make it back into the surrounding area. In the limited peripheral view of Burr’s welding mask helmet, he catches movement in an alley — three scavengers standing above a figure on the ground. Pug sees Burr turn. Together they head down the alley.
The scavengers look up. Their eyes go wide. They flee in terror, leaving the figure behind.
Crunch. Something breaks underfoot. Pug looks down — half-broken aviator sunglasses.
They turn the figure over. It’s Ben. Battered, bruised, bloodied. Beaten and left for dead. Burr lifts him onto his shoulder. Ben lets out a weak groan, blood occasionally dripping as they carry him.
“B..urr Is.. Pug.. with you?” Ben’s voice is faint, each word an effort. “Good.. that you’re both.. alright.”
He doesn’t know who attacked him — several men, unknown. His eyes are glazed, unfocused. His pulse is weak.
They head toward the Death’s Head checkpoint near Ben’s store. A heavily guarded outpost. Guards rush out, form a line, demand identification. They don’t recognize the armored figures. “NO FUCKING CLUE WHO YOU ARE! WHY DON’T YOU BRING IT UP AT ROAD CAPTAIN JODI’S SECTOR?”
The standoff continues. Guards demand surrender. Burr refuses. The guards are visibly injured — improvised bandages, broken table legs as splints, scraps of dirty cloth. Frightened, uncertain, leaderless. Whispers spread: “He said he’s the one that broke out!” — Burr’s reputation from the Pound breakout precedes him.
Burr gives a speech, stirring the hearts of the demoralized men. “THE COMMUNITY WE HAVE A CHANCE! WE CAN HOLD THEM BACK! THEY’VE GOT OUR FAMILIES!” Some are shaken. They don their masks, reinforce their wall, but will not yield passage.
Pug points behind them and yells “STRAY DOG!” — a good number of the guards turn in panic, spooked. The two agents speed-shuffle toward an alley, Pug faster in the lighter armor, Burr clanking in the heavy set. The guards do not pursue — only confused murmurs as they filter back through the checkpoint gate.
Shuffling quickly towards the Community, carrying Ben, they make their escape.

Summary
Sweating inside the suits, Pug and Burr find the walls of the Community up ahead. Ben’s pulse is still weak, his body growing colder. On the way, Burr tests the car battery maul — twisting the handles in opposite directions, electricity discharges between steel studs on the battery. Twisting back shuts it off.
At the gate, Burr calls up to the guards, helmet off, asking them to open up — Ben is injured. The guards peer down suspiciously at the armored strangers. “No can do! Strict orders! Gate stays closed until tomorrow! Come back then!” A snort from the other guard. “Cannot help you! Strict orders not to open gate!”
Burr argues. The guards mock: “Come back tomorrow, da? You can have tea time chat then!”
Burr presses the electrified maul against the fencegate. Electricity courses through the metal. One guard jolts back; the other’s grip refuses to open, taking the full shock. Dazed. Pissed. “Big mistake!” A whistle blows. Four more guards rush out of the guardhouse.
Burr prepares a makeshift bomb. Digging under the armor, he pulls out the metal can, glass bottle, can opener, and lighter. Cracks open the can, pours some liquid into it. Tears cloth from Ben’s shirt, soaks it in the mixture, leaves it hanging out as a fuse. Wraps the can tightly with duct tape.
On the wall, guards mix a white powder into a blue barrel of water. Pug watches from behind an abandoned car.
Burr lights the fuse. It burns almost instantly. He tosses the can up. The barrel tips — the solution pours down onto the street below. The ignited can falls into it. A small pop. Black smoke. “What kind of firework was that supposed to be?!”
The bomb fails.
Burr tries again — a fabric sling soaked in the liquid, lit and thrown into the barrel. A splash. Nothing.
The guards begin passing pails of solution along the wall.
Burr heads down the street, searching for a way around the gate. Guards follow on the inside, tracking him. A guard in a boonie hat emerges from the bunkhouse with a bag — he unfolds a hunting crossbow.
Burr finds where the gate meets the wall. He swings the maul. Concrete chips fly. Rebar bends. Through a hole, guards stab at him with improvised spears — kitchen knives on broom handles — but they clang off his armor. He keeps hammering.
Pug, behind the car, throws rocks to distract. The crossbowman finishes loading — aims at Pug. Pug keeps his head down. A bolt punches through the car hood, barely missing.
Burr tries to climb the wall. The heavy armor, the spears thrusting at his ankles — he falls backward into a wooden crate. Winded, unhurt. He removes his cloak, ties it to the hammer, tries to throw it over the top. Keeps falling short.
A bucket of solution flies through the hole, drenching Burr completely.
Burr keeps striking. The wall crumbles. The hole grows. Eventually it is just wide enough for a person to crawl through — without armor.
Burr begins to undress. Pug helps unstrap the heavy armor. Piece by piece, it comes off. Soon Burr stands in only his boxers, his improvised cloak, and the hammer.
He goes head-first through the hole. Rebar scrapes. Pug pushes from behind. He falls onto the other side — onto two rows of spike strips. The solution covering them. His cloak and body still damp.
A dozen guards stand in formation ten meters away. Wires connect the spike strips to a generator behind them. A guard connects two wires with pliers.
And through the open gate — two guards carry Ben into the compound.
“Stop where you are! Surrender! You’ve got no options left, scumbag!”
Burr looks at the guards. At Ben being taken. At the wires about to connect. He flips them the bird.
The wires connect. He lights up like a Christmas tree. Electricity courses through him — muscles forced rigid, arms locked in double defiance. Convulsing violently. The single moment stretches into an eternity.
The generator shuts off.
His body — smoke rising, skin blistered red, eyes rolled back — topples backward toward the hole.
Pug catches him. Grabs his arms. Pulls him through the hole, scraping against rebar. A sharp piece tears into the back of Burr’s right calf. His boxers tear but hold.
The guards inside start yelling, deploying. Pug has precious few moments. He lifts Burr into a fireman carry, grabs the bottom of the hammer, drags it along as he flees into the alleyways.
With the headstart, he outruns the pursuers. Lost in the alleys, carrying his unconscious partner.

Summary
As Pug escapes through the alleyways, Burr begins to feel colder on his back. His calf wound still drizzling blood. Pug stops, performs emergency first aid — wrapping the leg over and over with duct tape, creating a makeshift seal and bandage. Eventually, the blood stops pooling on the ground beneath.
They venture onward. In a shady alley, Pug spots an odd ramshackle stand — scrap wood and debris, with painted letters reading “TIME HEALS ALL THINGS.” A bell sits on the stand. Pug rings it.
A door slowly creaks open. An old man steps out — looking like a beggar in haggard rags, unshaven with a wild pencil moustache. “Ah..! Are.. you.. a.. cust.. omer..?” Each word painfully slow.
He trades in time. Explained in fragments: packages available — multiply the wearer’s remaining time by 2x, 3x, or 4x for the next 6, 12, or 24 hours. “Should.. he have.. an hour left.. if.. increased by double.. he would.. have two.. remaining..”
Pug picks an option. The old man nods slowly. “You.. seem.. down.. on.. your.. luck.. I’ll.. dis.. count.. it.. Only.. 50,000.”
He offers one of the cheaper-looking watches. Pug puts it on Burr’s wrist. The old man displays his own pocketwatch. Pug places the merchant’s watch atop Burr’s. The pocketwatch begins spinning slower.
The transaction is complete. The old man slowly collects the 50,000 Ahn. “A… pleasure… doing… bus… i… ness…” He creeps back into his building.
Pug faces two alleys. Left: downtrodden, trash bags, broken windows — rough but ordinary. Right: cleaner, but something about it makes his skin crawl. He takes the left.
Walking between derelict residential buildings, he feels watched. Movement in a window — empty when he focuses. The alley splits again. Right branch smells of blood. Left looks abandoned and destitute. He heads toward the blood.

Summary
Pug rounds a corner. The smell of blood hangs thick in the air. Three figures in the dark ahead: a form on the ground, a crouched figure hovering over it, and a lookout standing guard.
The lookout spots Pug. “Oi! You! Step out from there!”
Pug steps into full view with Burr draped over his back. The scene becomes clear: the crouched figure wears blue latex gloves and a medical mask, a scalpel in hand. Before him, a body with its chest cavity open. An organ harvester at work.
They eye Pug and Burr up and down. Pug says something — the harvester scowls. “Ha? The hell are you on about?” The lookout is dismissive: “Go on creeping then, jackass! Take your corpse and get out of here. We found this spot first.”
A pause. The lookout scoffs. “Fuck, not another one of you believers.” He points down the alley past them. “You won’t find shit. There is no ‘Healer of Light’. It’s bullshit.”
As Pug passes, the harvester calls after him: “Just some advice, though? Remember to take the guts too. Higher than normal rate right now. Can’t wait longer than a day to deliver ‘em though.” — they think Pug is a competitor carrying his own corpse.
Pug continues into the maze of twisting alleys, identical branching pathways. He gets hopelessly lost, winding around and around in the mess.

Summary
Eventually, Pug comes across a long, flat building. Above the entrance: a red cross. He pushes on the unlocked door and enters. A single-story dorm of some kind — a reception desk lit by flickering, barely wired fluorescent lights. On the chair where a receptionist would sit: a cage of white doves.
Pug taps the bell twice. The doves coo and flutter, distressed. Footsteps approach from down the hall.
A man turns the corner — bloody, once-white smock over a white dress shirt, sleeves rolled up. Small round spectacles, a medical mask. Mismatched latex gloves: one blue, one light red. He speaks to the doves in a foreign language, calming them, then faces Pug.
“Ahum. Hallo! You are here to zell, or for ze healing?”
He looks at Burr. “Euh.. He iz the patient? Mm.. Ja, I can vwork with zhis. How much can du afford to pay?”
Pug explains the situation. The doctor examines Burr, making mental calculations. “Mm.. That could vhork as a budget. Depending on severity of his vhounds, it may be a long time before he awakes.”
Pug asks about expedited treatment. The doctor thinks. “Uh.. Zhat’s a bit out of your price range, I believe… To stay close by, vhe can most likely shorten recovery to a vheek at best, should he respond vhell to all medications and trials agreed on the consent form. Vhe do not have the medicine in-house, and must order, so my best guess vhould be 250-300K.”
Pug agrees to 250,000 Ahn. The doctor changes the agreed amount on the form. “Okay! Please follow me, vhe have an available room for him right now.”
Burr is placed on an operating table. Assistants come in, gathering supplies. The doctor hands Pug a keyring. “Here you are, zhis is the key to zhis room, you are free to come and check on him at any time during his recovery.”
Four days pass. Pug visits Burr in recovery, then heads out to find a place to rest. He finds a rundown residential building, a room on the fourth floor with a broken lock. Finally, he rests. Barely six in the evening. He remembers Kent’s death, the day’s trials, the ruined relations with Death’s Head and the Community, losing Ben, and Burr nearly meeting his end once again.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-07/day-07-su.content:
Day 07 Summary

Timeline: July 23 to August 6, 2025

Day 07 covers a sprawling journey through the Fallen Wing underground facility beneath the Welfare Department building, followed by forays into Koller’s bunker, the community gate siege, and Burr’s hospitalization. The day begins with Pug descending alone into the depths and ends with both agents destitute in a rundown room and a clinic bed.
Key Locations: Fallen Wing underground facility (TV Room, Flesh-Hall, Cafeteria, Information Department, Armory, Spider Room, The Old Man’s chamber), BBQ restaurant, Koller’s bunker, Death’s Head checkpoint, Community gate, Time merchant, Organ harvester alleys, German doctor’s clinic

Verified Lethals





















































#TargetCause of DeathEquipmentNotesEncounter1Rat ThugStabbedPVC pipe spear with knifeKilled by Pug during Rune rescue7-5B2Rat ThugKnee broken, kicked against pavement—Killed by Pug during Rune rescue7-5B3Rat ThugNeck snapped—Killed by Burr during Rune rescue7-5B4Rat ThugChoked unconscious, used as bludgeon—Killed by Burr during Rune rescue7-5B5Rat ThugBeaten to death with unconscious rat body—Killed by Burr during Rune rescue7-5B
Notes: No human kills on Day 07. The Old Man survived the boss fight despite losing an eye — Pug and Burr escaped rather than finishing him. All five Rat Thugs were killed during the Rune rescue (7-5B).

Encounter Summary
Phase 1: The Fallen Wing (7-1A through 7-2I)

Covered in original Day 07 Summary

Pug descends into the Fallen Wing alone, navigating the underground facility beneath the Welfare Department. A series of tense encounters through dark corridors, locked doors, and the abandoned offices of the lower floors. Burr eventually catches up. Together they navigate bureaucratic obstacles, discover the manager’s apology letter detailing the building’s descent into cannibalism, find the hidden elevator keys, and prepare for the deeper descent.
Phase 2: Descent into Darkness (7-3A through 7-3I)
7-3A-7-3C: The Sealed TV Room & Burr’s Memory
Pug and Burr descend into the deeper facility. They discover a sealed TV room where Burr experiences a vivid memory — a fragmented vision of his past. The room is bathed in an eerie green glow from strange liquid permeating the facility.
7-3D-7-3F: The Flesh-Hall and Cafeteria
The pair navigate a horrifying corridor lined with organic material — the Flesh-Hall. Beyond it lies an abandoned cafeteria, long since stripped of supplies. The green liquid continues to appear in various forms throughout these areas.
7-3G-7-3I: Burr Found, Vending Machine, Secret Elevator
Pug finds Burr in a compromised state. They discover a strange vending machine that dispenses healing — a violet soda that miraculously restores wounds. Pug uses Martin’s Control Team ID card (retrieved earlier from the locker room) to access the machine. They find a hidden elevator leading deeper into the facility’s lower levels.
Phase 3: Information Department & The Old Man (7-4A through 7-4L)
7-4A-7-4C: Information Department, Forgotten Murderer, Samurai Armor
The pair enters the Information Department — a vast archive of records and data. They encounter the Forgotten Murderer, a ghostly figure in a noose, whose suit proves to be a significant item. They also discover a sentient set of Samurai Armor — partially damaged but still animate.
7-4D-7-4F: The Old Man Boss Fight
Deep within the department, they face The Old Man — a formidable boss. The fight is devastating:

Pug loses his left arm during the battle
Burr has his legs shattered
Despite the grievous injuries, they manage to escape rather than finishing the Old Man off.

7-4G-7-4H: Frantic Retreat and Vending Machine Healing
After barely escaping the Old Man, they frantically retreat through the corridors. They reach the same vending machine from earlier — the violet soda heals their worst wounds, allowing them to continue. Pug’s arm regenerates enough to function, Burr’s legs reform.
7-4I-7-4K: The Armory, Spider Room, Sir Tatum’s Appraisal
They discover the facility’s Armory, containing powerful items:

Skull Mace — A long cross with a skull and red thorns (later revealed as a relic)
Dark Funeral Suit — Two-piece suit with a choking black miasma
Glass Dagger — A dagger with a shattered shifting pattern (later revealed as a relic)
Lever-action rifle and other items

They pass through a Spider Room — a chamber infested with a swarm of spiders, from which Burr retrieves bloodstained bills. Sir Tatum (a mysterious figure) appraises their found items.
7-4L: The Exit
The pair finally escapes the underground facility, emerging back into The City. They are battered, exhausted, but alive — carrying several powerful relics and items.
Phase 4: The City Above (7-5A through 7-5B)
7-5A: The BBQ Restaurant
Pug and Burr stop at an unmarked BBQ restaurant to eat and recover. Here they encounter a mysterious woman in a raincoat — later revealed to be Lavender. She observes them but does not engage directly.
7-5B: Rescuing Rune
The pair come across a textile trader named Rune being attacked by a gang of Rat Thugs. They intervene:

5 Rat Thugs killed total (Pug: 2, Burr: 3)
Rune is rescued
Payment received: 400,000 Ahn from the grateful trader

Phase 5: The Community and the Siege (7-6A through 7-6C)
7-6A: Koller’s Bunker
They visit Koller’s underground bunker. Koller outfits them with new gear:

Car Battery Maul — A heavy electrical maul (Burr’s signature weapon)
Railroad Spike Dagger — Forged from a railroad spike, curved blade with brass knuckle grip
Light Armor Set — Long leather duster with metal and rubber reinforcement
Slim Dagger — Later revealed to be a ballistic knife

7-6B: Finding Ben
They find Ben beaten and bloodied near the Death’s Head checkpoint. The checkpoint guards confront them, leading to a tense standoff.
7-6C: Community Gate Siege
The community gate comes under siege. Burr is electrocuted during the fighting — severe electrical burns covering his body. Ben is captured by enemy forces. The siege ends with Burr critically injured.
Phase 6: Medical Emergency (7-7A through 7-7D)
7-7A: The Time Merchant
Desperate for resources, Pug seeks out a Time Merchant — paying 50,000 Ahn for time multiplication. Burr’s badly injured calf receives basic treatment.
7-7B: The Organ Harvesters
While navigating the alleys, they encounter organ harvesters — a grim reminder of The City’s brutality. They avoid engagement.
7-7C: The German Doctor’s Clinic
Burr’s condition deteriorates. They find a clinic run by a German-accented doctor who admits Burr for emergency treatment:

Payment: 250,000 Ahn
Treatment: Heliapoiesis and fibrous mechanite therapy (dual treatment, never trialed together before)
Time Skip: 4 days of recovery
Burr receives a mechanical healing implant (gestator)

7-7D: The Midnight Visitor
While Pug rests in his rundown room, a dark humanoid figure visits in the night. The visitor delivers tax documents — official paperwork showing Income: 100,000 SAU, Tax Due: 25,000 SAU. The figure departs without a word.

End of Day 07 State

Pug wakes and seeks food at a local spot, spending 1,000 Ahn. Refreshed, he tackles the problem of reaching Koller. He finds a small route through a run-down residential building to bypass the Death’s Head checkpoint and delves into the maze of alleys. The walk is uneventful, if time-consuming.
Koller greets him warmly from behind his surveillance feeds. He notices Pug’s new outfit and asks about Burr. Pug explains the situation. Koller seems surprised that a functioning hospital exists in this area.
Then the news. Two pieces of good, one bad. The good: Koller’s rival, the uptight and conniving man from the Fallen Wing expedition, has been attacked. He thought he contracted the Zwei Association, but they were impostors. He barely made it out alive and never reached his appraiser. The expedition members were cheated.
The compensation arrives in the form of two purple parcels. Oufi Association indemnity benefits, per Core Tenets Vol.4 Sec.2a1. Each contains 100,000 Standardized Ahn Units. Summary
Pug follows side streets, chasing rumors, until he finds a small workshop that deals in scrap weaponry. The kind of place that would sell something like the sword Finn carried. A man in a welding mask finishes his work, lifts the visor, and steps behind a counter.
Pug presents the Car Battery Maul. The welder looks it up and down. His mouth scrunches, his eyebrow furrows. He glances at Pug’s armor. “You lookin’ to offload this hunk of scrap onto someone’s porch?” A beat. “Just tuggin’ your leg. It’s a decent piece. How much?”
Pug asks for 100,000. The welder points at the weld marks on the metal. “Imperfect welds. Points of weakness. Looks more like a hobby project than a functioning piece of work.” He offers 15,000.
Pug demonstrates the electricity. The welder’s eyes widen. “Alright, it’s got a gimmick. It’s flashy. But you don’t know when it’s gonna blow on ya. Look at how big it is. No one’s swingin’ that properly. Twenty-five thousand. Or show me you can work with it.”
Pug turns to leave. The welder raises his voice. “Hey! Oi! You got thin skin or what? Fifty thousand!” Pug does not stop. The welder does not follow.

Summary
Time passes. Pug takes on small jobs through Koller’s listings, navigating the alleys with growing familiarity. After five days of deliveries, protection work, scavenging, and the occasional bit of information-gathering, he has earned about 32,000 Ahn after accounting for food and lodging.
The tax figure visits again in the night, delivering another letter. Pug does not open it immediately.
He checks on Burr at the clinic. The doctor greets him with enthusiasm. “Your freund may be waking soon.” Burr is in a patient gown, bandaged all over, his face wrapped to allow breathing. The doctor explains he has been responding remarkably well to the combined heliapoeisis and fibrous mechanite treatments. No one has ever agreed to trial both simultaneously. The doctor finds this fascinating and makes a joke about guts that does not land.
Pug sits with Burr. He begins drawing on the bandages. Halfway through the third drawing, Burr’s eye opens.
The doctor returns. Burr is awake, confused, trying to get up. The doctor examines him. Full range of motion. No itching, no swelling. He leaves them to talk.
Burr tears off his bandages. His skin underneath is completely fine. The burns from the electrocution have healed entirely, as though they never happened. He has stitches along his ribs, abdomen, neck, and back. He finds his blood-encrusted boxers in a cupboard, considers putting them on, and decides against it.
He tests his strength by lifting the hospital bed. It rises half a foot before he strains.
The doctor discusses payment. The total treatment cost is 250,000 Ahn. He offers two options: immediate payment, which incurs the Head tax on any single-day transaction over 100,000, or a payment plan, which avoids the surcharge and comes out cheaper overall. The doctor gives Burr a pill that will cause him to vomit the mechanites before they overbreed. “So you are not devoured and gutless.” Burr takes it without complication.
Pug works two more days. Between a parcel delivery and a protection job, plus some scavenging and free lodging, he earns well without spending a single Ahn. He wakes the next morning and counts out 111,600 Ahn gained.
Something is wrong. Over the past week, his body has felt weaker despite keeping up with activity and rest. His mind has grown fogged, as though the grey skies above had taken root in his thoughts. This morning, reaching for the hospital door, he notices his hands are lightly trembling.
Addendum: After waking Burr up, they pay their taxes and sort out the money and payments.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-08/day-08-su.content:
Day 08 Summary
Day 08 covers a short but consequential period — five days of Pug working jobs solo while Burr remains unconscious in the clinic, followed by Burr’s dramatic awakening, the discovery of his superhuman strength, revelations about his surgery, and Pug’s worsening mysterious symptoms.
Key Locations: Pug’s rundown room, Koller’s bunker, Scrap weapon workshop, Clinic (German doctor’s facility)

Verified Lethals





















#TargetCause of DeathEquipmentNotesEncounter————No kills recorded on Day 08.—
Notes: Day 08 is entirely non-lethal. Pug completes jobs without violence, and Burr remains hospitalized.

Encounter Summary
Phase 1: Recovery and Business (8-1A)
8-1A: The Weight of Purple
Pug wakes in his rundown room on the morning. Seeking food, he spends 1,000 Ahn at a local spot. He navigates through a run-down residential building to bypass a checkpoint, delving through alleyways to reach Koller’s store.
Koller’s News
Koller greets Pug cheerfully and delivers three pieces of news:

Bad news: The appraiser (Sir Tatum) was attacked the previous night by impostors posing as Zwei. The cargo was never sold — Pug and Burr have been gyped.
Good news #1: Koller’s “friend” finally got what he deserved — duped, soon to learn a lesson in humility.
Good news #2: Koller produces a small purple parcel from the Oufi Association — an independent contractor’s workers indemnity benefit. The letter cites Oufi Core Tenets Vol.4 Sec.2a1: 100,000 Standardized Ahn Units (SAU) as compensation due to the contractee’s failure to fulfill their end. A second identical package for Burr is also provided.

Pug inquires about side jobs. Koller brings up available listings. Pug departs with money and opportunities ahead.
Key event: Oufi indemnity — 100,000 SAU for Pug, 100,000 SAU for Burr (sealed, cannot be opened by Pug).
Phase 2: Failed Sale (8-1B)
8-1B: The Welder’s Offer
Pug attempts to sell the Car Battery Maul at a scrap weapon workshop. A welder in a welding mask inspects it:

Initial offer: 15,000 Ahn
After Pug demonstrates the electrical discharge: raised to 25,000 Ahn
As Pug walks away: raised to 50,000 Ahn

Pug continues walking. The maul remains unsold.
Phase 3: The Week of Jobs and Burr’s Awakening (8-1C)
Time Skip — Five Days
Pug takes on small jobs from Koller. Some require expertise of others, others prove impossible (finding a cat here and there). After five days, he nets 32,000 Ahn after food and lodging.
Second Letter from the Mysterious Figure
The night after the first visitation, the dark humanoid figure appears once more, delivering another letter. Contents unknown.
Hospital Visit
Pug visits the clinic to check on Burr. The German-accented doctor greets him excitedly, saying Burr may wake soon. Burr lies bandaged all over, face covered except for mouth and nose. The doctor explains Burr responded remarkably well to both heliapoiesis and fibrous mechanite therapy simultaneously — never trialed together before. He estimates Burr will wake tomorrow.
Alone, Pug draws penises on Burr’s bandages. Midway through the third one (on Burr’s cheek), Burr stirs — one uncovered eye cracks open.
Pug shows Burr the tax documents: Income 100,000 SAU, Tax Due 25,000 SAU.
Time Skip — Two Days
Emboldened by Burr’s awakening, Pug follows up on more jobs: a smooth parcel delivery, and a protection job where he threatens off Rats before an altercation occurs (client buys a heavy lunch in gratitude). Ample scavenging, free food, no lodging costs. Pug nets 111,600 Ahn over these two days.
Pug’s Worsening Symptoms
Over the days, Pug notices his body feeling weaker despite proper care. His mind grows foggy, thoughts slowing. On the final morning, his hands tremble lightly as he reaches for the hospital door.
Burr’s Check-Up
Pug arrives at the hospital to find commotion — Burr is awake, panicking, trying to get out of bed as assistants try to calm him. The doctor arrives holding a dove named Syracuse. He dismisses the assistants and examines Burr. Burr claims he feels fine.
Full Recovery Revealed
Burr tears off his bandages — his skin underneath is completely fine, as if the burns never happened. Testing his strength, he lifts the hospital bed half a foot with one hand. He finds stitches at his ribs, abdomen, neck, and right back — the gestator implant surgery sites.
The Missing Dove
The doctor is looking for Syracuse — the dove is missing. Pug puts his ear to Burr’s stomach and hears something rumble and move inside. The doctor gives Burr an emetic pill. Burr vomits mechanites into a bucket.
Payment Discussion
The doctor presents the bill. Options: a payment plan (cheaper overall) or immediate payment (more expensive due to Head Tax on amounts over 100,000 paid in a single day). The amount remains undetermined.

End of Day 08 State

Summary
The bills are settled. Tax forms, hospital charges, treatment costs, the immediate-payment surcharge. All of it. Pug’s balance, which had climbed to over 800,000 Ahn during the week of recovery, drops sharply. But nothing remains owed.
The two of them step outside the clinic. The air is cold. The fog hangs low. And something is wrong.
It starts subtly. Clammy skin. A light perspiration that has nothing to do with the temperature. Pug notices his hands trembling first, a faint vibration he cannot will to stop. Burr feels it too. They check independently. No fever. Skin cold to the touch. No facial drooping, no arm misalignment. Nothing that points to a stroke or a poisoning.
Just the trembling. And a fog in the mind that was not there before.
Burr scans the street. No one is watching. No one is following. The alley is empty.
They head out without any specific leads. The crumbling concrete and rubble on the pavement irritate Burr’s bare feet. He needs something to cover them. Down an alley, they hear a fire crackling. They round the corner and find a barrel fire with two individuals bundled in layers of tattered clothing. The two look over, then break eye contact, staring somewhere near the agents but not directly at them.
Burr asks if they have anything to spare for his feet. Shoes, cloth wrappings, anything. The two do not engage, continuing to look down. At the continued questioning, they exchange a worried glance. One reaches into a jacket and pulls out scraps of old, torn clothing, gingerly extending them without making eye contact. Burr wraps the cloth around his feet. It is not pretty, and not stable. But it will hold.
Something has changed in them, and neither knows what. They turn back toward Death’s Head territory.

Summary
People on the street give them a wide berth. More than before. The reputation has spread, or perhaps it is the way they look. Either way, no one approaches.
They pass the hospital and head toward familiar ground. The warehouses near Death’s Head territory come into view, and they are different now. Looted. Destitute. The streets emptier, the buildings hollow. A clattering noise from inside one of the warehouses draws Burr’s attention. He peers through the door and finds three men searching through boxes. One wears a leather vest, another an open-faced motorcycle helmet with a bandana, the third a tattered leather jacket.
Burr announces himself with a cheerful “Housekeeping!” and asks for shoes. Sandals, flip flops, anything. The men are nervous, cautious. “You just want some shoes? We don’t want any trouble, man.” The one in the helmet drops down and starts undoing his laces. They drop the shoes on the floor and toss them over without making eye contact. “Just give us a minute to gather some stuff, and we’ll be out of your way, alright?”
Burr puts the shoes on. They are an improvement over the cloth wrappings from the barrel fire people. The agents leave the warehouse men in peace and turn toward Death’s Head territory.

Summary
A Death’s Head checkpoint ahead. Two guards in leather vests and white shirts, one with a cracked helmet. They see the agents approaching and back up, splitting off from the entrance. Giving a wide berth in case the agents decide to come through. Burr dances through, giving them fingerguns. They hold the same distance for Pug. No collections box this time. No one asks for anything.
The territory is emptier than before. Fewer patrols, fewer people on the streets. A few Death’s Head members hang around building entrances, watching warily. No one moves to stop them.
Near the square where the Stray Dog fight happened, two streetlights hold silhouettes. Bodies, suspended by their feet. Burr identifies them first: the local Death’s Head leader, the woman with the shotgun, and her second-in-command. Both headless.
The Death’s Head headquarters is abandoned. Desks covered in paperwork, prison cells empty. Pug searches the armory side while Burr checks the barracks. A woman in a medical mask and kitchen apron is tending to the sleeping men in the bunks. She tells them the Stray Dogs have been squeezing the territory dry. Everyone is leaving before the Dogs come back. No one knows where the Dogs are, and no one who knows would say.
She gives them a lead: a man named Maisner, fond of his drink, who used to trade information with the patrols for food. He lives in the alleyways.
The armory is barren. A few broken scraps of armor, unwieldy pipes, broken pool cues. Nothing worth taking. The agents leave the territory around 14:00 and follow the woman’s directions into the alleys.

Summary
The alleys lead them back to familiar ground. The area where they first encountered the motorcycle and fireaxe man, limping from those on the rooftops. Men in tattered, layered coats watch from the edges. None of them look directly at the agents, but the feeling of being watched is constant.
Following the woman’s directions, they reach a small square. No sign of Maisner. A shack nearby smells of something cooking. Burr knocks. The occupant is hostile. “Fuck off! I ain’t no Maisner! He’s over across the Pit!” He refuses to engage, yelling about ingredients and money. They leave.
A drunk man sitting outside a building with a bottle points them down an alleyway. His speech is incomprehensible, but the gesture is clear. They follow the path until it opens into a destroyed area. A crater where a building used to be. Rubble descending into the ground. Burned cars. On the other side, a makeshift shack of scrap metal and wood.
Burr’s foot slips on crumbling ground near the edge. Pug grabs him, catches himself as rubble breaks away, and pulls Burr up to solid ground.
On a makeshift porch overlooking the pit, a man in a thick jacket and flatcap sits on a ratty couch surrounded by bottles and cans. He sizes them up. He knows Maisner. But Maisner does not meet just anyone. They need to prove they are trustworthy first. The man owes a cook named Lester some money, and Lester will not see him because of it. If the agents bring the man a bowl of goulash, the man will introduce them to Maisner. His stomach growls. Alternatively, they could bring Lester some ingredients. Either way, getting on Lester’s good side gets them on the man’s good side.
The two agents scale down into the Pit to scavenge for food scraps and ingredients.

Summary
The Pit is a communal dumping ground. Bags of trash, building wreckages, burned cars. Burr rummages through the garbage and finds scraps: mostly empty cans with a spoonful of food each, stale bread butts, a half-eaten corndog with something green growing on it. Pug finds a tied-up restaurant waste bag, puffed up from trapped gases, liquid sloshing inside. Best not to open it.
Pug climbs out easily, bag held high. Burr struggles with the cans and the hammer. A single can nearly falls back down. He catches it, but two others slip from his arms and tumble into the abyss. They go back down, collect them, and scale the pit again. The man on the couch watches, wide-eyed, and raises his bottle in a nod of respect.
They bring the haul back to town and knock on Lester’s door. He opens the eye hatch, takes the scraps, and examines them. “Not bad for your first haul.” He takes Pug’s bag and retreats inside. Some time passes. He opens the door, eyes red and streaming, snot running down his nose. The waste bag contents hit harder than expected. “That’s the good shit.” He apologizes for his earlier hostility.
Lester explains he is about to finish up a batch of goulash that just needs a final touch. He will make them something special, but he needs meat. He points them across the street to an old woman named Vagna, a “magic woman” who can summon meat. The plan: bring Vagna a bowl of goulash as an offering, and she will provide the meat in return. Lester already has enough from a previous batch to give them a bowl for Vagna. Once they bring back the meat, he will finish the current batch properly.

Summary
Vagna’s shack is decorated with Christmas lights and a broken fog machine. Inside, an old woman is sobbing. Her cat, Mittens, has died today. She cannot give her a proper burial. She does not ask them to bury the cat. She simply states her grief and begs them to treat the corpse gently.
A thud behind them. They turn. A dead cat lies on the ground. Vagna has already moved away from the door. There is no explanation for how the cat appeared. It was not there a moment ago. They get an idea. The goulash needs meat, and… meat has just appeared.
They make a fake grave from a chunk of rubble. A marker, nothing more. The cat itself is not inside it. They wonder about what they have just done.
They bring the cat to Lester. He takes it inside. Some time passes. He calls out. The goulash is ready. He opens the door and hands out a tray: four bowls of goulash and two shot glasses of a pink liquid. One of the bowls is much smaller, barely containing any meat. “Tell him he owes me that fuckin’ money! Slap the shit out of him if you gotta!” Lester shouts after them.
The goulash itself is good, but the pink liquid is something else entirely. An alcohol of some kind. Burns on the way down, sickeningly sweet, but delicious. The vapors linger in the mouth afterward. And they feel rather confident for reasons neither can explain.

Summary
They bring a bowl of goulash to Vagna’s door and knock. “YES? WHO IS IT?” The voice is loud, sharp, and old. They announce themselves. “OH MY! HOW GENEROUS!” The door creaks open and a bony, withered hand reaches out from the unnatural darkness within and takes the bowl. She thanks them warmly. Then she asks what they needed. They mention the cat.
She is confused. “WHAT CAT DID YOU MEAN?” The door closes. Rustling. It creaks open again. The bony hand extends, placing a dead rat in Pug’s hand without ceremony. “OF COURSE!” The door closes. The footsteps recede.
They leave the rat at Lester’s shack, knock, and depart for Maisner’s.

Summary
The two cross the path next to the Pit without incident. Maisner is already on his porch, and he can smell the goulash before they reach him. He peers down at the bowl, then at the two remaining bowls and the shot glasses. “What’s the meanin’ of this?”
Burr tells him Lester sent them. Maisner goes pale. “Wh- You told him I-, that Maisn- That I’m Maisner’s bud?!” Then he notices the shot. “Huh?! Peach alcohol? The hell are you two talkin’ about?” He warns them it is dangerous, then immediately offers to take it off their hands. Burr makes a deal: the shot in exchange for information about the Stray Dogs.
Maisner resists. “You want me to rat on the Stray Dogs? For THAT?” But the temptation is too great. He asks for a sniff first. Burr blows the vapor in his face. Maisner’s eyes go wide. Without a word, he reaches for a notepad and pencil and starts scribbling directions. He rips off the paper and folds it up.
He gives them a taste first, then hands over the note, then drinks his own half-shot. “Hhhoooo.. That’s some good hooch.” He takes the other shot and pours it into a large glass bottle of his own liquor. “Yeah, sure. On the house.”
The intel: The Stray Dogs operate in packs. Bosco, the Pack Leader who fought in their territory, was one. Pack leaders do not cross each other’s territory. They answer to someone higher, but no one knows who. The Dogs use specialized tattoo ink, different brands, some made in-house. The tattoos are flashy but only work when activated, in short bursts. Their accessories are the real threat, allowing “cloak and dagger shit” while looking like part of the tattoos. Catch them off guard, and the tattoos are useless.
Maisner finishes his bowl and mentions a contact who knows more, someone who also has a grudge against the Dogs. To meet this contact, the agents need to raid one of the Dogs’ tattoo parlors and bring back proof. He recognizes them from the pharmacy incident. “Oh! You’re the two idiots that tried to steal from the pharmacy? That was crazy! It’s alright! We all start from somewhere, eh?” He tells them to take care and come back anytime.
They return the bowls to Lester as evening falls. The temperature drops. Pug is fine. Burr feels the cold more than he should.

Summary
The two follow Maisner’s directions, setting off immediately through the slum quarters. The ruined buildings gradually give way to undisturbed streets, the classic winding of backstreets they have grown accustomed to. A small side street marked by the directions appears ahead, clear and unremarkable.
As they proceed, Pug spots a man standing in an alleyway to their right. From behind, he wears a threadbare, tattered business suit. His head is slightly slumped, staring at the ground. The agents pass the alley warily. He does not react.
Burr continues walking. His foot strikes a glass bottle. It skitters forward, clatters across the pavement, tips over, and rolls into the street. They both pause, glancing back. Nothing emerges from the alley. They continue onward, nearing the end of the directions.
Then Burr feels it. Something uncanny about his footsteps. He freezes. Another footstep sounds in perfect sync with his own, and stops when he does. Looking behind him, the street has curved but still offers a long view back. No one is visible, but the sound had definitely come from behind, from some distance.
His senses heighten. He hears and feels nothing save Pug’s presence. He taunts whatever follows to reveal itself. No response.
He begins to skip down the road. Pug hears only Burr’s skipping. But Burr, faintly, hears the other footsteps resume their normal walking cadence, now even further away. He stops, pivots, and sprints toward Pug. Pug sidesteps, watching him oddly as Burr sprints past. The streets are so empty that his footsteps produce an echoing sound. He runs until he disappears from Pug’s view.
And then he sees it. The man from the alleyway, walking down the sidewalk toward him. This time, Burr can see his face. His eyes are wrapped in bandages, completely covered. He does not seem to notice or mind Burr’s increasingly loud footsteps closing the distance. He continues walking directly toward Burr, his mouth moving, but whatever he says is inaudible.
Pug, meanwhile, freezes as he hears a similar footstep nearby. It is coming from inside the building next door, one floor above. The footsteps descend a staircase. Pug leaves his position and heads toward Burr, glancing over his shoulder. No one emerges to follow.
Burr activates his hammer, holding his ground. The blindfolded man continues his steady approach, gait unwavering, muttering inaudible words. When he is about twenty paces away, he stops. The muttering continues, barely audible. Burr hears a countdown. Pug relays it.
They break off running. The man makes no move to follow. As they pass the building Pug heard the footsteps from, the door stands open. Yet no one appears on their way back.
Approaching the end of the street, they find it terminates in a dead end. Fortunately, one of the buildings bears a sign: “TATTOO PARLOR.” Burr barges inside. Pug waits outside.

Summary
Burr barges into the lobby of a building. It is empty. Pug, having heard no sounds of breakage and seeing no blind followers, heads inside to regroup. The lobby is unremarkable, but Pug notices several signs on the building’s exterior. Most are blacked out. He recalls there were five names in total, four darkened, with the Tattoo Parlor listed as the fourth. The first read “SUMMIT ACCOUNTING.”
They head upstairs. The second floor is an abandoned office space. Flashlight reveals empty desks, scattered dust, and stacks of crumpled paper. They continue climbing. The fifth floor is locked. Burr smashes the handle off and forces it open. Inside: more stacked papers and desks, bearing the name “BLUE ROCK HOLDINGS COMPANY.” They check the fourth floor. More of the same. Blue Rock Holdings again.
On the sixth floor, light seeps from beneath the door. They open it normally. A small counter sits before them, with an older woman behind it. She looks up, surprised. “Hello! You have appointment? Tattoo parlor up one floor. Hair salon.” They thank her and compliment the shop, noticing a younger woman working on a client whose head is wrapped in a damp towel.
The seventh floor door is heavily decorated: spray-painted purple and black, nails driven into the doorframe to resemble studs. Inside, a heavily studded man wearing a kitchen apron and backwards baseball cap is finishing a tattoo. The buzz of the needle fills the room. “Take a seat! Be with you in a sec!” He does not look in their direction.
They wait. After ten minutes, the artist steps back. His client rises, revealing tribal-type markings freshly inked on his arm. The client wears a tank top and cargo pants with a chain on his belt. He looks like a leaner version of the Stray Dog they once fought. When he sees Burr, he freezes, eyes scanning him up and down. “Yo… Holy shit, you’re prepped, dude! Sick. First time ain’t too bad. Hope it goes well.” He leaves.
The artist cleans his station and walks over. “Aight. What can I do ‘ya for?” He confirms he has several different inks, though not the Stray Dogs’ own brand. They come to him. He asks if they are in the market.
The agents inquire about pricing. The artist explains: 3,000,000 Ahn for a full double-pattern whole-limb enhancement of all four limbs. Single-pattern whole-limb runs 250,000 per limb normally, 200,000 for repeat customers. He does not work on credit without insurance. A Syndicate or Fixer license would help, but the agents have neither.
He offers a compromise. He will cover a single-pattern whole-limb enhancement on credit, with the condition they pay double when they return. They decline.
“Alright. Here’s what I could do. We can do Tiger Stripe and Leopard Print. I’ll put the print in between the gaps of the stripe. Shouldn’t mess up the network. Most common ones we mix.” But they lack the funds. He nods. “You two take care, ay? Come back when your pockets are flush, I’ll set you guys up good.”
Burr insults him on the way out. The agents descend the stairs, passing the hair salon. As they head down, a door opens on the floor above.

Summary
The door to the tattoo parlor swings open and two voices speak in unison from the sidewalk outside: “Zero.” One is the man in the tattered business suit from the alleyway, eyes still wrapped in bandages. The other is a teenage girl in a hoodie, hood pulled low over her eyes. Neither blocks the agents’ path. They stand on opposite sides, like sentries awaiting an arrival.
Burr speaks out. The blind man and the girl both lift their heads in mild surprise, but offer no immediate reply. The girl speaks first. Her voice is quiet, uncertain in a way the blind man’s movement never was. “Ah.. Are you the wayward one?” the man asks. His words carry an odd formality, as if reciting from memory. “The wayward patient that has lost their way.”
The girl steps forward, her gait lacking the confident stride of her companion. She reaches into her hoodie and produces a newspaper clipping. Before handing it over, she tears it in two and offers the smaller piece. It depicts a restaurant that won a local award some years back. BBQ meat and rice. Praised for being delicious yet affordable. “I was told to,” she says, with the tone of someone fulfilling an obligation they do not fully understand.
The man speaks next, his words measured. “I was told to speak this, upon meeting the wayward patient.” He pauses. “‘Return to the place of loss and sorrow, and you will reclaim that which you have lost, before the ‘morrow.’”
Burr thanks them and moves to leave. The man, as if remembering something, produces a folded piece of paper. “Match the loudest footsteps upon hearing the shattering of glass.” Another paper follows. “Exit the alley and turn right, whereupon walk twelve hundred paces, or until the door closes.” When asked where these instructions came from, the man says it was handed to him that morning while getting groceries. The girl says it was placed in her mailbox a few days prior.
Pug, growing more bewildered by the answers to his questions, catches up with Burr. The two retrace their steps toward the dungeon, the weight of cryptic instructions settling over them like dust.

Summary
As the agents make their way through the streets, they spot a pair of thuggish-looking individuals surrounding a smaller woman in an alley. Without hesitation, both agents charge. Burr pauses mid-stride, calling out, and Pug freezes mid-slide. The two thugs turn, expressions shifting from annoyance to confusion as they register the armed men bearing down on them.
“What are you two doing?” one of them asks, bewildered.
Burr explains that he assumed they were robbing her and wanted to make sure she was safe. The thugs stammer. “N-No! She’s.. our sister!” But the woman and the other thug exchange a look of such transparent insincerity that even the participants seem embarrassed by it.
The woman speaks. Her delivery is flat, theatrical in the way someone who has never acted might attempt it. “Kyaaa. I’m in duress. These villains are robbing this fine maiden.” She scrunches her eyebrows as if to convey distress. Even the two men appear appalled by her performance. She seems more concerned than offended by their reaction.
“What?! Why would you do that? You’re cruel! What kind of miscreant comes across a beautiful maiden such as myself and threatens them?”
Burr points at her and accuses her of not being human. She pauses, considering this. “E-Eh? What do you mean?” Feigned shock. The two thugs attempt to slink away into the alley. She gazes back at the agents nonchalantly, apparently bored by the entire exchange. She explains she was looking for healing herbs when the men approached her with a proposition. She quotes them back in the same flat monotone: “Hey there little miss. You looking for a good time? You should come with us.”
“THAT’S NOT THE WAY WE MEANT IT!” one protests.
The confirmed bandit trails off, admitting they hoped she might fetch some money. He offers to hand her over. “Wait! You can have her! We don’t need the money anymore!”
The woman looks at Pug. “Double it.”
Burr advances. The thugs draw weapons. One has a shiv fashioned from scissors; the other carries a broken adjustable wrench. Burr launches into a spinning roundhouse kick that catches the shiv-wielder in the solar plexus, sending him flying backwards, the scissors clattering from his hands. His companion, momentarily distracted by the spectacle, fails to raise his wrench in time. Burr’s elbow crashes into his jaw. The wrench clatters to the ground. He collapses like a sack of potatoes.
Burr picks up the scissor shiv and finishes both men. Their brief careers in the City come to an abrupt end.
The woman extends her hand toward Pug. “Where’s my twenty?” She had bet on Burr. She takes the scissor shiv and pockets it. Then she clears her throat, as if preparing a rehearsed introduction. “The two of you have had your luck turned around! For you’ve stumbled upon… K… The Great Karla the H.. the Magical Healer!” She bows, her expression unchanging. Pug applauds politely.
She examines Burr’s injuries, finds them beyond her current means. She can heal, but direct resurrection is illegal, and she does not wish to be smited by the Gods. She sighs. “I can see what I can do, there’s some other methods.” She agrees to accompany the agents. “The Great Witch Karla does not look away from the poor, disheveled, pitiful and destitute.”
She tells Burr he is grossly tall. The three sally forth together.

Summary
Karla snaps her fingers in front of both agents. “Ah. Are you done zoning out? I’m getting hungry.” She looks toward Pug expectantly. Burr mentions he is broke and suggests a restaurant.
They arrive back at the small BBQ restaurant where they once ate. As they duck beneath the entryway curtains, a familiar figure sits at the counter with his back to them. A figure in a raincoat. Burr sits to his left, with Karla beside him, and Pug to the raincoat’s right. “I gotta find myself one of those raincoats,” Burr remarks. The figure turns. It is an unfamiliar young man with a blindfold on.
Burr does not recognize him. Pug immediately scans the room. Behind them, at a table near the doorway tucked out of sight, a young woman wears a hoodie with lavender hair beneath and a cloth facemask. Three sets of meals sit before her, steam rising, the same dish they once ordered. A twinkle in her eye, as if suppressing laughter, as she meets Pug’s gaze.
The agents rise. The blindfolded man also rises, removes the raincoat, places it on a nearby table, and walks out without a word. The young woman coughs. “Ah. Could you pass that over to me? That is mine. I thought it would be funny to have the Messenger wearing it.” She takes the raincoat and gestures to the seats. “Here, for you three.” She moves one of the meals to an empty seat, which Karla fills instantly, as if she had fully expected this development.
The woman is cornered in the back of the restaurant. She explains why she sent the blindfolded people: they knew where the agents were and could deliver directions. She asks if they know why she invited them. Burr says for her to give them cool stuff. She stifles a scoff. “Well, that is not entirely wrong. I wanted to offer you an opportunity for that ‘cool stuff.’”
She has caught wind of where the “cool stuff” is at. She wants to recover some of what they have lost. “A mace with a skull, and a dagger made of shattered glass. At least those are the ones I have heard of.” She wants them to continue working together. Additionally, reports suggest the Enkephalin retrieved from the facility has surfaced, and she suspects it is with the same groups holding the weapons.
Burr asks about Enkephalin. “Ah. Sorry. It looks like a green liquid. Always bubbling? There were capsules of the stuff down in the facility.” She looks concerned. “You drank it? Like straight? …I can see why you seem to have been hospitalized. It is a miracle you made it out of the facility at all.”
She lays out the situation. A certain group of people, out of their element, hold the supplies and equipment. They plan to sell tomorrow. The agents could either raid their hideout tonight, or intercept during transport tomorrow and risk encountering the buyers. The buyers are people interested in this kind of equipment, of which even the knowledge is not widely known.
Pug looks at Karla. “Hey kid, how old are you?” “800.” “I am the Great Witch, Karla. Sorry. Healer.” She cannot fight. She heals after battle. She tried healing mid-battle once and healed the wrong person. “It did not go well.”
The woman extends her hand. “Lavender works. That sounds cute.” The four rise. Lavender dons her raincoat, hood shrouding her face. “Safer that way.”

Summary
Lavender leads Pug and Burr through a maze of side streets and alleys, deliberately avoiding main roads to maintain a low profile. After some time navigating the back ways, she stops before a corner and gestures ahead. “You two are up. Clear the way.”
Burr charges around the corner without hesitation, only to slam head-first into a chainlink fence stretched across the narrow alley. He bounces back, dazed. On the other side of the fence, three hoodlums snicker at the spectacle — until Burr grabs the metal fencing with both hands and rips the entire section off its poles with sheer brute force. The hoodlums’ laughter turns to panic.
“W-Woah.. W-Who are you? We don’t want any trouble!” They backpedal, offering money, begging for mercy, completely confused about who these people are. One of them, trying to defuse the situation, mentions that a couple days ago he saw “a bunch of guys came through with boxes and construction supplies.. Lotta shit.. Pretty protected too.” He points in the direction past them — the same direction Lavender was heading.
Lavender shrugs. “Dunno. I don’t know who they are. I just wanted the fence out of the way.” She hadn’t known there were people behind it. The three hoodlums flee without further incident. Lavender redirects: “Ah. This way. Got directions.”
The rest of the journey is uneventful, though the agents notice the walls along the route are sporadically sprayed with bright, vibrant colors — various splashes of paint in no discernible pattern.
No combat occurred. No kills, money, or items were gained or lost.

Summary
Lavender leads the party through the apartment complexes. The buildings have storage units and garages on the bottom floors, giving the area a rough, industrial feel. She points ahead to a squat, barricaded building — windows covered in sheet metal, iron bars on the doors. Docker’s compound. The pawnshop is a converted garage unit run by Docker, a local pawn dealer who holds the skull mace and glass dagger.
The party splits. Burr approaches the front door. Pug slips around to the back.
At the front, Burr hefts the car battery maul and swings into the reinforced front door. The impact reverberates like a gong through the building.
At the back, Pug finds three men: a pawnbroker with a shaved head and a black eye, an armed guard, and a customer holding a box. The guard peels off to investigate the noise from the front. The customer asks if Docker is still buying. “I gathered all I could find, but it should be good quality.” Pug creeps up on them in silence.
Inside, someone screams at Burr to stop hitting the door. Footsteps pound up the stairs. Burr breaches the door, chases the man up the stairs, drags him back down, and curbstomps him on the steps.
Pug snaps the customer’s neck from behind — kill one. He grabs the pawnbroker by the collar and holds a knife to his back, dragging him off-stage. “Where is the stuff?” The pawnbroker cracks: “I don’t have access to it! Only Docker has the key! Top floor! Penthouse!” Pug stabs him through the back of the neck — kill two. He heads through the door to meet up with Burr.
Burr finishes off the guard on the stairs — kill three.
The box of unknown value is left behind on the pawnshop floor. No money or items are recovered. The party advances toward the second floor.

Summary
Burr breaches the front entrance of Docker’s compound after the gonging assault. A man flees up the stairs — Burr catches him, drags him back down, and curbstomps him into the ground. He then ascends to the second floor.
Three armed individuals are already on the second floor: one with a metal pipe, one with a wooden bat, and one with a rusted machete. They were heading toward the stairs when they saw Burr coming up — they scramble back, caught off guard. Burr charges forward without hesitation.
Pug catches up from the garage level, stepping over the dead pawnbroker’s guard, and ascends the stairs behind Burr.
Burr’s hammer combo is devastating and swift:

Man 1 (metal pipe): Hammer to the side of the head. Skull cracked. Drops instantly.
Man 2 (wooden bat): Hammer to the ribs. The bat is useless as protection — ribs shatter. He crumples to the floor, unable to move.
Man 3 (rusted machete): Uppercut to the chin. The hammer’s trajectory disconnects the neck from the spine. Blood spews as he collapses.

All three bodies hit the floor just as Pug steps onto the second floor. Man 2 is still alive on the ground, whimpering in agony, unable to move. Burr finishes him off.
A second set of stairs continues upward toward the upper floors.
Before Burr can ascend further, a speaker system crackles to life. A voice — Docker — begins speaking through it, agitated and panicked:

“Stop! Stop! What do you want?! Who are you?!”
”…Okay, okay! You want the relics? I’ll give you them! Just stop killing!”
“No! I’m sending someone down there. No way I’m going with you crazy fucks! I don’t know who you are!”

The speaker goes silent. A brief countdown begins from somewhere in the building, but before it completes, something crashes loudly outside — a heavy impact that shakes the structure.

Summary
Pug continues up the stairs toward the penthouse. Burr bolts back down to investigate the crash outside. Burr reaches the outside first and finds a destroyed wooden crate with smaller boxes scattered inside. He starts opening the shoebox-sized containers — folders, journals, notebooks covered in crayon smiley faces, stick figure drawings of families, diaries. He senses something wrong, steps back just as another crate comes crashing down from above.
Meanwhile, Pug reaches the top floor and finds a metal gate blocking entry to the penthouse. He pries the gate enough to break through and slips inside. The penthouse walls have been knocked out to create a single massive room. A heavyset man in a grungy wifebeater and thick leather jacket lounges on a reclining couch — Docker. Four other men occupy the room: two dragging boxes toward a window, two standing nearby. One guard wears a large puffy coat that conceals his body.
Docker notices Pug. “What? What do you want? Your shit is outside already!” He asks about Pug’s friend. “Where’s your friend?” / “Is he opening the boxes?” Docker squints, motions to the men by the window to shut it. “Your scary friend’s down there. I got a scary friend of my own.” He gestures to the puffy jacket guard. “Why don’t you just stay right there?” The puffy jacket guard cracks his neck.
Outside, Burr tugs at a car door, finds leverage with a sledgehammer, and cracks the door off after a few swings. He begins working toward the penthouse window.
Inside the penthouse, four guards post up: a beanie-wearing guard with a baton, the puffy jacket guard (hands in pockets), a masked guard with a crowbar, and a turtleneck guard with a tanto knife. Pug notices the turtleneck guard has black lines running up and down his forearms — tattoos. A Stray Dog connection?
Pug throws his machete at the turtleneck guard, who ducks. The baton guard charges, his body suddenly moving faster, one eye glowing red — enhanced ability. The baton crashes down on Pug’s knife, rattling his hand. Pug deflects and tears his knife across the baton guard’s throat, killing him. The crowbar guard charges; Pug stabs his wrist, then jams the knife through his jaw — second kill.
A metal fist swings past Pug’s head — the puffy jacket guard has brass-colored metal fists. The tanto guard charges from behind, slashing across Pug’s back, but the armor blocks it. Pug fires his ballistic knife into the tanto guard’s chest below the shoulder, wounding him. The wounded tanto guard stands near the puffy guard, who raises a boxer’s stance, metal fists in full view.
Pug taunts the metal-fisted guard, slides under his arm, and slashes the tanto guard’s ankle. The tanto guard throws his weapon aside. “I.. I give..” Pug holds him hostage, knife to throat. The puffy guard charges anyway and punches the tanto guard in the face — friendly fire, killing his own man. The impact sends the tanto guard’s head crashing back into Pug’s; both fall.
Pug is dazed on the floor. The puffy guard grabs his throat: “Not so fast now, are you?” The window shatters — a distraction. The puffy guard glances back. Pug fires his ballistic knife into the puffy guard’s forehead — third kill.
Silence. Then Burr’s voice from outside: “THESE BOOKS FUCKING SUUUCK!”
Pug approaches Docker, who stammers: “W-What the fuck.. just happened..?” Docker surrenders immediately, hands over a key necklace that opens a storage unit outside. Pug drags Docker downstairs.

Footsteps approach outside as the encounter ends.
