Pug descends from the penthouse, dragging Docker by the collar. Burr is outside, still finishing his work — prying the last of a destroyed gate off its hinges. The two agents converge. Docker, defeated and trembling, looks between them.

Docker: “Y-You guys.. W-Who the hell do you work for..? You guys are.. really fucking with the wrong guys.. you know? Do you know who we were supposed to sell these relics to?”

He hesitates, then confesses:

Docker: “You guys are messing with the Accepted.”

The name means nothing to the agents, but the weight in Docker’s voice is unmistakable. Docker gestures toward a storage unit just outside the compound. The key necklace around Pug’s neck — the one Docker surrendered — opens it. They escort him to the unit.
Docker unlocks the roll-up door and pulls it open. Inside, the space is cluttered with several crates of varying sizes, stacked and packed with care.

Docker: “O-Okay! Okay. I uh.. Packaged these real good, you know? It.. It will take some time.”

He starts unpacking, opening crates methodically. He picks up journals and notebooks, dumping them out onto the floor — old records, personal logs from the facility, irrelevant to what the agents actually came for.
Then he opens a larger crate.
Inside rests a long cross mace. The weapon is unmistakably relic-grade: a heavy iron skull caps the head, bound in red thorns that wrap around the neck of the mace and trail down the shaft. The thorns are sharp, the skull grinning. Two yellow canisters are packed beside it — Enkephalin.

Docker: “A-Ah… That’s the one you wanted, yes? Ah fuck.. I knew accepting that deal wasn’t any good.”

Docker opens a smaller crate. Inside is a shattered glass knife — the blade is fractured, shifting, its surface pattern constantly rearranging, as if the glass is alive. Beside it sits one more yellow Enkephalin canister — three total.

Docker: “No more relics. None of that. Don’t want any part of that spooky shit anymore.”

Burr reaches for the Skull Mace. He grabs it by the shaft, his fingers wrapping around the red thorns. The thorns prick his skin — they are sharp enough to penetrate, yet they do not draw blood. An odd sensation blooms across the top of his head, like a crown of thorns pressing against the inside of his skull from within. The feeling is not painful, but immediate, unnatural.
Docker notices nothing amiss, too focused on his own dread.
As the agents begin to gather their findings — the Skull Mace, the Glass Dagger, the three canisters — the sound of footsteps echoes from outside the storage unit. Someone is approaching. The timing is too precise to be coincidental.

Summary
With Docker’s surrender, the party unlocks his storage unit. Inside, they find the glass dagger and three yellow Enkephalin canisters — Green bubbling liquid, retrieved and carried by the group.
As they emerge from the storage unit, half a dozen individuals approach. They look like ordinary civilians but wear bright colored clothing — sewn patches of colored fabric, tie-dye shirts, green towels draped over their shoulders. Each carries a belt with a book at their side. None appear to have weapons except for one man: he steps forward with papers tagged to his clothes and a rusted knife in hand.
“We heard your calls of despair and anguish. Tell me, brothers, what is going on here?”
His eyes fall on the relics. “Those.. relics, you say, were yours? You found them then.. Have you communed with them..?” His eyes widen. “Tell me, brother, what did it feel like..?” Whispers ripple through the others behind him.
“You must come with us. We can help you commune, to accept it deeper. We seek to collect these relics, and help those who resonate with them most, commune and reach the heights they were meant to.” He claims not to know what other relics the collective possesses, but assures that the collective will gather them, and that Pug and Burr can commune with them. “We simply ask that we can witness your ascension.”
When asked if staying with them is required: “No. You will not need to stay. After you commune, you will go out and do as you please, and paint the City in your own colors, as She meant it.”
“Everyone is Accepted.”
“We will go where the relics go.”
Docker, still present, trembles. “Can.. Can I go..?” He seizes the chance and flees, leaving the agents with the Accepted.
The party heads back to Karla and Lavender. At the sight of the Accepted accompanying them, Lavender tenses up and reaches into her raincoat. ”..What’s going on?” / “That’s.. very much not a good idea.”
The Accepted members grow agitated at her words. Lavender lowers her voice: “I.. can’t speak of it here. Not with them.”
Pug takes Lavender aside to speak privately. Meanwhile, Karla remarks, “The Accepted seem really fun. They remind me of my magic.”
After coming up with a plan, Pug takes the mace from Burr, and hands the weapons to Lavender.
Burr takes Karla and runs off toward the restaurant. Pug says they will meet Lavender at the restaurant as he follows suit.

Summary
The two agents, having split up with their newfound allies, head toward the area. Walking for over an hour, the buildings grow taller and the fog hangs lower. The air feels thinner and colder. They venture into completely unexplored territory — more destroyed buildings, rubble, and destroyed cars, far more destitute than the abandoned yet structurally sound apartment buildings of Death’s Head territory.
Pug, warm enough in his jacket, watches Burr shiver in his blood-soaked gown with virtually nothing else. The two banter between each other, making jokes about cannibalism, and as it turns weird, they eventually awkwardly stop, walking in silence.
As the fog hangs down lower, they spot a light flickering in an alleyway. Approaching the light, they find a barrel fire with markings of a small hideout: a collapsed, broken tent, dirty towels and cardboard on the ground for bedding, and a duffel bag on the floor.
Burr approaches the duffel bag, squatting down and unzipping it. In the dark, lit only by the fire’s flickering light, he catches a glimpse of a wallet and eagerly grabs for it. Pug hears a metal twang snap. A metal trap springs and catches deep into Burr’s forearm, its teeth stabbing into his flesh and crunching down.
Pug’s alarm bells ring as he glances around for threats. Burr pulls on the trap, careful not to make things worse, and feels a chain snaking through the bottom of the bag, under the collapsed tent and cardboard, deeper into the alleyway heading left.
Before either of them can react, a crossbow bolt sprouts out of Burr’s upper left arm, the force staggering him. Burr recovers and begins stomping down on the bear trap, prying it open with his right hand and left foot. Meanwhile, Pug spots a brief glimpse of movement vanishing from a second story window in the building immediately opposite the alleyway.
Pug immediately sets off to chase down the crossbow user, dashing across the street. By the time he reaches the other side, Burr has finished untrapping himself, blood seeping out where the trap had impaled. Burr picks up the bear trap and his sledgehammer, venturing deeper into the alleyway to check where the chain leads.
Pug opens the door to the building — a destitute, abandoned residential building. He spots a staircase immediately to his left and elevator doors further down. He presses the elevator button. It does not light up. Holding his spiral knuckleduster knife in his right hand and the flashlight in his left, Pug ventures up the stairs.
He reaches where the sniper had been: a collection of tables pushed together with blankets covering some, right in front of the window. Empty cans, bottles, and a half-eaten bag of chips suggest the sniper had been equipped to remain there for some time. Following the way the discarded blankets had been skewed towards, Pug climbs higher. The dust on the stairs leading to the third floor is noticeably disturbed — a fresh set of footsteps continuing upward but not setting foot onto the third floor.
Following the footsteps, Pug reaches the fourth floor, then the fifth, then the sixth. The weight of his inventory and metal-plated coat wear him down as he ascends, getting winded. Eventually he reaches the roof, right after the eighth floor. The door opens onto a flat rooftop where the fog hangs so low it’s hard to see even a few meters ahead.
Hearing the tail end of a high-pitched whistling noise, Pug moves cautiously toward the sound. He sees a thin, pole-like silhouette. Approaching it, he confirms his suspicions: a length of cord going across and down the street. He unlatches his belt and hooks on. The line creaks and sways under his weight, straining, but he has a secure grip.
Pug takes a step off the 8-story building and puts his whole weight on the straining line. He begins to zipline across, the line bowing and swaying, wind chill against his face. About two-thirds down the line, he hears a startling cracking and crashing noise from where he had come. The line goes slack, losing its tension while he’s in the air.
Initially aiming towards the 6th floor, Pug makes a split-second decision to not grab at the 5th floor as it passes by. He crashes through the window of the 4th floor. The glass shatters, turning into scattered glass and glass dust as he makes an ungraceful, tumbling landing. Bits of glass scatter all over him and get in his clothes. Aside from some scrapes and bruising, he’s remarkably okay. He hears footsteps from below, coming up. Pug hides in a darker part of the stairwell and waits.
Meanwhile, Burr rounds the corner and finds the end of the chain wrapped around the leg of a dumpster, padlocked. Disappointed at the lack of foes pulling him, he smacks the chain with the sledgehammer, crunching it and breaking a link. The bear trap and long length of chain are now free.
Burr hears a whistling noise above him. Something comes heading towards him — he doesn’t have enough time to properly react, only enough time to step out of its way as it crashes to the floor. The sound of glass shattering as his vision fills with yellow dust or powder. On his wounds, it tingles and burns. His eyes begin to have a burning sensation, watering up and obscuring his vision. He closes his eyes and stumbles back.
Something heavy but not particularly hard thunks into the back of Burr’s head and knocks his head forward. A plastic bottle, half-filled with liquid, rolls away. Opening his eyes, he sees an unmarked plastic bottle with the wrapper taken off, the liquid mostly clear. He pours it into his eyes — aside from a bit of grit and sand, it seems to be water. He successfully cleans out his eyes.
Burr then pisses in the bottle. He winds up the chain and bear trap, swings it around, and lets it fly forward. The bear trap hits the edge of a window, hits the pressure plate, snaps, then falls to the ground. He winds up again and lets it fly once more. The bear trap flies through the air, crashes through a window, and clamps down on something. He tugs and it drags something. He puts weight on it and begins to slowly ascend. He hears something cracking and snapping from above as the bear trap returns with a chair leg.
He hears a secondary crash upstairs. Heading up, even after the secondary crash, Burr continues up the stairs. Eventually ascending a few floors, he sees a silhouette in the dark on the stairs ahead.
Burr throws his bear trap forward at the figure while the figure jumps up into a dropkick. The figure kicks forward, directly onto the pressure plate. The trap clamps down onto the figure’s ankles as they kick, pushing the trap into Burr’s chest. The two of them begin tumbling down the stairs, getting caught up in the chains.

Day 15 Summary

Timeline: December 6, 2025 to June 5, 2026
Time has lost all meaning. The characters have lost track of what day it is — hence the 1X- prefix and the title “Or is it.” This “day” spans six months and nearly 20 encounters.

Day 10 covers three distinct phases across six months: hospital discharge and the fall of Death’s Head (Dec 6), the Stray Dog investigation through messengers and oracles (Jan 3-17), and the explosive reunion with Lavender and the assault on Docker’s compound (Jun 5). Major revelations include Lavender’s identity as the raincoat figure, the nature of Enkephalin, and the introduction of The Accepted faction.

Verified Lethals

Total Day 10 Lethals: Burr — 5 kills. Pug — 4 kills. Grand total — 9 kills.

Encounter Summary
Phase 1: The Fall of Death’s Head (Dec 6, 2025)

Time Skip: ~4 months (Aug 11 to Dec 6, 2025). Burr has fully recovered from all physical injuries. Both characters have been living in The City. Pug’s symptoms — body weakness, mind fog, hand tremors — have persisted and worsened.

1X-1A: An Unknown Dawn (Dec 6)
Leaving the hospital on Dec 6, both characters pay off their bills — the mysterious tax forms and the hospital bills — leaving them with nothing. Both independently notice strange new symptoms: clammy skin, hand tremors, cold to the touch (no fever). They head toward Death’s Head territory. At a barrel fire, two bundled individuals reluctantly give Burr torn cloth scraps to wrap his feet.
1X-1B: Housekeeping (Dec 6)
Walking through Death’s Head territory, the warehouses they once knew are now looted and destitute. Three scavengers are searching through boxes. Burr announces himself: “Hello!~ Housekeeping!” The scavengers are terrified — more of the Stray Dogs than of Burr. One tosses him a pair of shoes. They point the way forward.
1X-1C: The Pound Falls Silent (Dec 6)
They approach a Death’s Head checkpoint — the guards back up and split off, giving wide berth. No toll collected.
At the Pound, they find two bodies hanging by their feet from streetlights — decapitated. Burr identifies them as the local Death’s Head leader (shotgun woman) and her second-in-command. The headquarters is abandoned. Desks and paperwork left behind. The prison cells where Burr was once kept are empty.
Key Intel: A young woman in a medical mask and kitchen apron explains everyone is leaving before the Stray Dogs return. She gives them directions to Maisner — an information broker who trades info for food and drink.
Death’s Head status: Leadership dead. Territory in decline. Members fleeing.
Phase 2: The Stray Dog Investigation (Jan 3-17, 2026)

Time Skip: ~4 weeks (Dec 6, 2025 to Jan 3, 2026)

1X-2A: The Pit (Jan 3)
Following directions to Maisner, they navigate alleyways to find Lester’s shack (a cook who shooes them away) and The Pit — a massive crater where a building used to be, now a communal dumping ground. Maisner sits on a makeshift porch overlooking the Pit. His test: bring a bowl of goulash from Lester.
1X-2B: Scavenging in the Pit (Jan 3)
They scale into The Pit to scavenge ingredients for Lester. Burr finds food scraps. Pug finds a tied restaurant waste bag (fermented, gases building). Lester is intoxicated by the fumes when they bring it — “That’s the good shit.” He agrees to make goulash, but needs one final touch: meat. He sends them to Vagna, an old magic woman.
1X-2C: Vagna and the Cat (Jan 3)
Vagna is grieving — her cat Mittens just died. Burr offers to bury the cat. A dead cat thuds behind them. Pug has an idea: cat goulash. Lester accepts the fresh meat. They make a fake grave for Mittens. Lester delivers four bowls of cat goulash and two pink liquor shots (temporary confidence boost).
1X-2D: The Summoning (Jan 3)
They return to Vagna with a bowl of goulash. She asks what they need. When they ask her to “summon” something, she produces a live rat. They leave the rat at Lester’s door and head to Maisner.
1X-2E: Maisner’s Intel (Jan 3)
Maisner smells the goulash before they even reach him. He demands the peach alcohol (which they don’t have) — Burr blows his breath in Maisner’s face instead. Maisner scribbles down directions.
Stray Dog Intel:

Bosco (the one who croaked in their territory) was a Pack Leader
Packs have grunts; Pack Leaders don’t mess with each other’s territory
Pack Leaders answer to someone higher, but no one knows who
Different Stray Dogs have different tattoos, different brands, some made in-house
Tattoo weakness: Only works when activated — short bursts. Catch them off guard, “you put that mutt down.”
Accessories can mimic tattoo powers — “cloak and dagger shit”
Maisner knows someone with a hard-on for the Stray Dogs — if they fuck up the parlor and bring back something good, he’ll put them together
Directions lead to a Stray Dog tattoo parlor

Time Skip: ~2 weeks (Jan 3 to Jan 17, 2026)
1X-3A: The Blindfolded Man (Jan 17)
Following Maisner’s directions through the slums, they encounter a man in a tattered business suit standing in an alley. Burr feels something uncanny about his footsteps — hears his own non-skipping footsteps continue after he starts skipping. The blindfolded man approaches, mouth moving inaudibly. About twenty paces away, he begins a countdown. They flee. A door they passed is now open. They reach a dead end — the “TATTOO PARLOR.”
1X-3B: The Tattoo Parlor (Jan 3-17)
The tattoo parlor is on the seventh floor of a building (Summit Accounting, Blue Rock Holdings, a hair salon below). The artist recognizes Burr’s prepped state. Pricing:

Full body: 3,000,000 Ahn
Per limb pair (two-pattern): 750,000 Ahn
Single limb single-pattern: 250,000 Ahn (200,000 for regulars)

No credit without insurance, Syndicate backing, or Fixer license. Over ~2 weeks, the artist offers one single-pattern whole-limb enhancement on credit (pay double next time). Burr considers it but ultimately declines. They leave.
1X-3C: The Prescripts (Jan 17)
Exiting the building, they encounter two figures: the blindfolded man and a teenage girl in a hoodie. They deliver messages:

The girl: Tears a newspaper clipping in half — gives the smaller piece showing a BBQ restaurant award. “I was told to.”
The man (oracle message): “Return to the place of loss and sorrow, and you will reclaim that which you have lost, before the ‘morrow.” (The Pound/square where Kent fell.)
The man’s prescript: “Match the loudest footsteps upon hearing the shattering of glass.” “Exit the alley and turn right, whereupon walk twelve hundred paces, or until the door closes.”

Both received their prescripts mysteriously — the man that morning while getting groceries, the girl in her mailbox days prior.
1X-3D: Karla the Great Witch (Jan 17)
Retracing steps, they spot two thuggish individuals surrounding a smaller woman. Burr intervenes, killing both scavengers (solar plexus strike, elbow to jaw, finished off). The woman introduces herself: Karla the Great Witch (800 years old, healer). She claims she doesn’t fight — she heals after battle and can “yell really really loud.” She joins the party.

Time Skip: ~5 months (Jan 17 to Jun 5, 2026). Karla now travels with the party. Pug acquires a machete during this period.

Phase 3: Lavender, Enkephalin, and the Relics (Jun 5, 2026)
1X-4A: Lavender’s Offer (Jun 5)
Karla is hungry. They go to the BBQ restaurant from the newspaper clipping — the same unmarked restaurant from 7-5A. Inside:

A blindfolded young man in a raincoat sits at the counter
A young woman with lavender hair sits at a table with three steaming meals

The blindfolded man takes off the raincoat and leaves. The woman claims the coat: Lavender reveals herself — she was the raincoat figure from the facility (7-5A, 7-4K). She sent the blindfolded messengers.
Lavender’s Offer:
She knows about “lost” items from the facility: a skull mace and a glass dagger, plus Enkephalin (green bubbling liquid in capsules). “You drank it? It’s a miracle you made it out.” The items are held by Docker, a local pawn dealer planning to sell tomorrow. Two options: night raid on their hideout, or intercept transport (risk of buyers).
Karla introduced properly: She confirms she’s a healer, 800 years old. She accepts “Lavender” as a nickname. The four head out together.
1X-4B: Clearing the Way (Jun 5)
Lavender navigates through side streets and alleys. She stops before a corner — Burr charges into a chainlink fence, rips it off the poles. Three terrified hoodlums behind it offer intel: Docker’s operation is heavily protected, arrived a couple days ago with boxes and construction supplies.
1X-4C: The Pawnshop Garage (Jun 5)
They reach Docker’s compound — a barricaded apartment building. Splitting up: Pug to the back, Burr to the front.
Burr slams the maul against the reinforced front door — gonging sounds. Pug finds an open garage converted into a pawnshop with three men: a pawnbroker, an armed guard, and a customer. During the confusion:

Pug snaps the customer’s neck silently
Pug stabs the pawnbroker through the back of the neck — learns only Docker has the key (penthouse, top floor)

1X-4D: The Second Floor (Jun 5)
Burr breaches the front door. A man runs upstairs — Burr catches him, drags him down the stairs, curbstomps him. On the second floor, three armed men await (metal pipe, wooden bat, rusted machete).
Burr’s Rampage:

First man: skull crushed with maul
Second man: ribs crushed, finished off while whimpering
Third man: uppercut disconnects neck from spine

Docker’s voice on speakers: “Stop! Stop! What do you want?! I’ll give you them! Just stop killing!”
1X-4E: The Penthouse (Jun 5)
Pug ascends to the top floor. Burr checks outside — finds a car door, rips it off with the maul for use as a weapon/shield. Pug reaches the penthouse: Docker on a reclining couch with four guards:

Baton guard (enhanced, red eye)
Puffy jacket guard (metal fists)
Crowbar guard
Tanto guard (Stray Dog tattoos)

1X-4F: The Penthouse Fight (Jun 5)
Pug fights all four guards solo while Burr is outside:

Baton guard: Charged enhanced; Pug deflects with knife, slashes throat
Crowbar guard: Pug stabs wrist, jams knife up through jaw
Tanto guard (Stray Dog): Pug fires ballistic knife into his chest; used as human shield — killed by puffy guard’s metal fist (collateral)
Puffy jacket guard: Pug fires ballistic knife into his forehead — thunks deep into head

Losses: Machete (thrown, not retrieved), Slim Dagger / Ballistic Knife (fired twice, lost). Back slashed but armor blocked damage.
Docker surrenders: “Here! This is it! Storage unit outside!” He gives Pug a key necklace.
1X-4G: The Storage Unit and The Accepted (Jun 5)
Docker leads them to a storage unit. Inside: journals, crates, and the relics:

Skull Mace — Long cross with red thorns binding and adorning a skull. When Burr grips it: crown of thorns sensation inside his skull. Does not draw blood despite thorns penetrating.
Glass Dagger — Shattered glass with a shifting pattern
3 Yellow Enkephalin Canisters — Green bubbling liquid

The Accepted Introduced:
Half a dozen individuals arrive — civilians wearing bright colored fabric patches, carrying books at their sides. Their leader: “We heard your calls of despair and anguish.”
They ask if Burr has communed with the relics. When he confirms the crown of thorns sensation, their eyes widen: “You must come with us. We can help you commune, to accept it deeper.” They seek to collect relics and help those who resonate with them most. “Everyone is Accepted.”
Lavender’s Reaction:
Lavender tenses upon seeing the Accepted, reaching for her weapon. She warns: “That’s very much not a good idea.” She cannot speak freely in their presence. She is very wary of them.
Karla’s Reaction:
Karla seems to enjoy the Accepted: “They remind me of my magic.” She suggests resting with them.
Departure:
Docker is released and flees. Burr takes Karla and runs off. Pug tells Lavender they’ll meet her at the restaurant. The three head to the restaurant. The Accepted follow — now bound to the relics.

End of Day 10 State

Summary
The three — Pug, Burr, and Karla — arrive at the BBQ restaurant as the owner is locking up for the night. The sky has darkened; it is approximately nine or ten in the evening.
Burr shouts for her not to close the door. She looks at them quizzically. “Eh? Sorry, no more customer today. We close.”
Pug and Burr argue-whisper among themselves. They bring up the option of paying to spend the night. “Eh… How much you two pay? What group you belong to?”
Pug offers 10,000 SAU. The older woman looks between the three of them. “OK, you two here earlier. Just no cause trouble. Come in. Once I close door, I no open no more.”
She holds the door open. Pug pays the woman. Burr and Karla follow her upstairs to the residential area. Pug waits downstairs, waiting for the rendezvous with Lavender.
Time passes. The sky continues to darken.
Night falls in the Backstreets.
Pug begins to hear a rumbling from afar as the ground begins to shake. Outside the windows, the dark side street illuminates by a light red glow from afar.
With the First Wave’s arrival imminent, Pug heads upstairs to the residential units, having decided it unlikely Lavender would appear until morning.
Over the course of the night, the feverish feeling and chills throughout Pug’s body increase in intensity. He wakes with dry mouth, nausea, dizziness, and a gray pallor visible to Burr. Burr suffers to a lesser degree, but still worsens — sweating, chills, and some dizziness, as if catching the flu.

Summary
The trip is primarily uneventful, but as Burr reaches the chainlink fence he and Pug had destroyed the night before, he almost walks past it. Where the fence used to be, there is now a solid wall. Where there should be a slim alley between two buildings, it appears as though the two buildings had always been a singular structure — the wall weathered and matching the texture and supposed age of the surroundings.
Stumped, and realizing he is lost, Burr decides upon the sensible approach: he begins to wander randomly.
He heads in a direction that feels familiar, yet enough differences make him uncertain. Some walls are painted bright yellow, appearing to be more recent paint. Smiley faces are painted on walls here and there.
Off in the distance, Burr hears faint singing. He decides it is a good idea and wanders toward it. As he navigates the alleys, the walls become brighter and more colorful.
The singing grows louder. It is almost like a chorus or choir — several voices singing together. He cannot make out the words, but he feels the emotion: anger, grief, sadness, jealousy, pain. Twangs that pluck at his heartstrings.
As he gets closer, a light green tint appears in the air. The fog hangs lower. The tint, the fog, clash against the brightness of the paint and fabrics strewn about. The singing grows louder, and his senses pull in more and more information.
Where is Lavender? Do they have her? Thoughts swirl through his head, focusing on his anger. The anger amplifies.
He steps into an open plaza. The yellow walls appear red to him, breathing heavily as his vision narrows and reddens. A dozen or so individuals in makeshift robes — stitched and quilted fabrics — sing before him. He cannot make out the words, but each is singing of their own experiences.
He continues to approach. The air hangs lower and thicker. Green mist swirls around the choir. Bright, blinding lights come from beyond the mist — he feels stared at by blinding glares. He blinks. The choir seems smaller, the environment far larger, closing in and surrounding him. His anger grows, a rippling pressure in his chest.
A figure begins to approach out of the mist. A larger man in a thick canvas duster, blue stab-proof vest, cargo pants, and combat boots. His back to Burr, peering into the mist, scanning for something or someone. Three more figures appear behind him. The description is familiar — painfully so. This is the Cocky Raider Leader from the apartment building, the man Burr killed with a shovel and brass knuckles on Day 1.
“Keep it careful boys. He should be here somewhere.”
“It’s an easy job, just don’t get clipped like the other two.”
The fog surrounding Burr thickens and coalesces into a hallway — the apartment building lobby from that night. Three men push forward, more following the larger man. Some open doors, enter rooms. All armed with knives, pipes, improvised weaponry. An empty hallway to his right. The men to his left.
He watches them approach. Three meters. Two meters.
“He’s here!”
A flash of red — a fire extinguisher pauses in front of him, thrown from his right. It explodes into fog and smoke. The same fire extinguisher Pug grabbed from the lounge chairs. The same smokescreen. The same moment.
A bullet flies past, striking into one of the men behind him.
“Ah, damnit. It’s out.” A pistol clicks. A familiar voice — Pug’s voice.
In snapshots, Burr watches another man rush forward — a man in tattered business pants and a white shirt, having removed his red tie and jacket. Pug. He charges into the three men in the smoke. The apartment raid replays before his eyes, fragment by fragment, pulled from memory by the green fog and the choir’s song.
Eventually, Burr snaps out of his daze. He is walking by familiar alleys. The choir is nowhere to be found, seen, or heard.
He sees two familiar figures ahead — Pug and Karla. They wave in recognition.
Burr pushes the hammer against his leg and delivers himself an electric shock. The electricity courses through him, muscles tightening, jaw clenching.
The shock ceases. His head feels remarkably clearer.
Pug and Karla stare at him in confusion.
Burr recounts his experiences — the cult, the singing, the world of memories. The apartment raid, replayed as if it were happening again. He believed it was a few minutes, yet an hour has passed. He did not find Lavender.

Summary
The three of them — Pug, Burr, and Karla — head out, deciding that wandering aimlessly might prove productive in the search for Lavender. The acrid smell of burning flesh reaches them before anything else. They follow the scent through alleys and streets until they stumble upon a small clearing.
Scorchmarks surround the area, lightly glowing with embers. Several bodies lie on the ground and against nearby buildings. The charrred robes identify them as members of the Accepted. One has his head blown completely off, robes scorched. Another is missing an arm. A third has a chunk of his side and center of his back blown out, exposing his spine and charred lungs.
The trail continues down a small alleyway — blood spatters and char marks indicating the fight and pursuit continued as combatants moved. The embers glow brighter, suggesting more recent activity.
They step out of the alley into a small shopping district with two streets passing between buildings. There, they find Lavender. Her raincoat is torn to shreds, partially melted, splattered in ash and blood. She clutches her arm, unarmed, breathing heavily.
In front of her stands one of the Accepted. His left arm has been blown off, one eye missing — scarred and blown out, teeth visible beneath the charred flesh of his lower jaw. In his right hand, he holds the Skull Mace. A crown of thorns sits upon his head, and his robes have turned red and white.

Summary
Pug hands Karla off and Burr charges in toward the Accepted. The man turns, his empty eye socket beginning to glow with radiant light, the skull mace also glowing. “Thaaaats… nooot… yooouuuurss…!” he murmurs.
Burr launches the hammer. It strikes something solid a millimeter away from the man’s head — not fully connecting, as if hitting an invisible barrier. The man’s head knocks backwards from the impact regardless. But the mace crashes into Burr’s side. Bones snap and crunch. A burst of blood shoots from Burr’s mouth. He remains standing, but heavily knocked to the side, vision blurred, blood dripping from his nose and ears.
Burr drops his hammer and charges again on all fours. The man swings the mace once more, chanting under his breath, eye socket and skull mace radiantly glowing. It strikes Burr’s opposite hip — the bone shatters and pulverizes. Blood seeps from his eyes.
Burr pushes forward, tearing at the man’s throat with his teeth. A barrier blocks briefly, then almost shatters. Burr’s teeth tear into the flesh and rip out a chunk. The man shoulder-checks Burr to the ground. Burr cannot move from his shattered pelvis.
The man reaches up to his neck. Blood gushes and does not stop. He drops to his knees. He lifts his hands, clasps them together, closes his remaining eye, and begins to pray. The skull mace and his eye socket begin to glow brighter.
The mace begins to lift off the ground, as if by its own will.
Pug, in a mad dash, drives the railroad spike knife right between the man’s eyes. His skull careens backwards. The praying ceases. Arms drop. The glow fades from his socket. The mace clatters to the floor. The thorn crown disappears. His robes return to their normal, dull but colorful colors.
Burr lies on the floor, blood from his nose, mouth, ears, and eyes. Lavender collapses to her knees, shivering.

logs/pugburr/encounters/day-16/16-2e.content:
Encounter 15-6D: [Title Pending]

Burr-only encounter. Dream sequence while unconscious.

Burr

Does not exist within Her realm.

Summary
Burr awakens in a stone-block prison cell. His feet are manacled to the floor. A wooden bench and a small hole in the corner are the only furnishings. A window covered in iron bars sits high above, near the ceiling, but provides no light. It is night outside.
A voice questions why this child has been placed here. A dark cell, iron bars separating the child from the hallway. He sees no one in the opposite cell, yet a presence is felt in the room beyond the wall. Two rooms in the dark. The sinner, and the parishioner.
The child utters his defense. No response is heard or felt. Perhaps he has been wrongfully accused? To survive is not a sin. The child has only done what was needed. There has been no wrong.
He speaks again, but the parishioner gives no answer. An outward questioning, for the child has not sinned. It was simply his nature.
The manacles break. “He who has not sinned deserves no chain.” The door swings open. The hallway is available.
But from the far end, another child stands. Crown of thorns upon his head, mace in hand. He speaks, and no evil is heard. The mace is raised. “For without sin, there can be no repentance. And then, who will propagate the hundreds of good deeds?”
The child’s words fall on deaf ears. If justice is blind, then the holy be deaf. The way out is blocked. An immovable ideology.
The child continues to speak, unmoving. Just as the other child remains still, mace in hand. The child walks forward, intent on leaving. The child with the mace stands as he approaches. Mace raised. Forward. He continues to walk. He reaches the door. Locked. Sins unresolved, incompatible ideologies.
The child forgives the other, believing it to be his place to grant forgiveness. For he who has not sinned shall grant forgiveness. And the child has only ever done what was needed to survive.
The child reaches for the mace. The figure allows him to grasp it. The thorns disappear. The light fades.
The child speaks falsehoods, claiming his acts as sin, yet believes them not to be. He is struck — smacked across the face with an open palm. He continues to speak, to acknowledge his acts as some kind of “wrong.” Yet does the child believe them to be wrong? Not by the judgement of the parishioner, but his own. They have only been right acts.
He hears the door unlock behind him. The once-wielder of the mace is gone. Inside the cell the parishioner assumedly resided, a single skull lays on the floor, out of reach.
The child leaves, mace in hand.
Changes

Summary
Burr blinks his eyes open. He finds himself standing, his hands duct-taped around a streetlight pole. Pug’s duct tape binding holds strong. The pole does not budge.
Pug hands him the mace, still wrist-strapped with duct tape. Burr grabs it. Tugging again — no difference.
Burr remarks despondently on the mace’s lack of skull and thorns. Pug says it still has them. Burr does not see them.
Pug cuts Burr free after Burr says “Please” and Pug remarks that he is a “Good boy.”
Burr begins to chant and say different words to try to re-activate the mace. Nothing happens. Meanwhile, Lavender begins to stir. Burr has been down for about two hours.
Burr grabs where the skull and thorns used to be. His fingers pass through empty air.
He strikes the pole with the mace. A resounding clang. Neither the mace nor the pole appears damaged.
Lavender sits up. “Why are you hitting the infrastructure? Are you trying to pay a fine?” She blinks in surprise. “Let’s slow down a sec. What happened?”
Burr explains his dream sequence to Pug and Lavender, catching Lavender up to speed. “I really did not need to hear the last part.”
She examines the mace. “I don’t know. I haven’t heard of anything like that happening. I guess you broke it? It sounds to me like you were in the attunement process. Typically it gets violent, long before whatever happened there. Generally you either attune successfully, or it corrodes and assimilates with your psyche. It sounds like it rejected you. Or… incompatibility. Maybe it’s not you, it’s the mace?”
She pauses. “I don’t know. I just thought it would be funny comparing it to a relationship.”
Burr berates the mace, throws it on the floor, and walks away. Lavender retrieves it.
Burr decides to destroy the Accepted.
Pug asks Lavender what happened. She explains: after the three departed, she played along with the Accepted for a bit. When night fell and the first wave began, she tried to evade. They pursued, and combat continued throughout the night. As the third wave concluded, she got the jump on them after they overextended. She engaged and took most of them out. However, one Accepted had cornered her, retrieved and forcefully attuned to the mace while she fought the others. They fought until the agents arrived.
She kept the glass dagger safe — it is still where she left it, behind the bed in her room. She nods.
She reveals that relics tend to have matching suits that come along with them. “You were wearing one down in the entombed building, before.” She recognized the one Burr was wearing. “I don’t have any leads on that one yet.”
She says she should go retrieve the dagger. “That’s part of our deal for those canisters you retrieved.”

Summary
All four — Pug, Burr, Karla, and Lavender — set out to retrieve the dagger. Karla stares at Burr with a deadpan expression as he verbally abuses the mace. Before she turns to keep walking, Pug catches a look of pity on her face.
They approach an apartment building when half a dozen rough-looking individuals appear in the street. Improvised weapons on their hips or held low.
The tallest one looks over. “Oi! You lot got any money?”
“We’re collecting funds for the neighborhood watch. There was a big fight last night, families don’t feel safe.”
“All right. Take care. You need a jacket?” Burr walks off.
The man looks at Pug expectantly. “Anything helps.” At Pug asking how much, the man says he doesn’t have a set price.
Pug counts out bills and hands over 5,000 SAU. His eyes widen. “Oi.. Are you sure? This ain’t coming with anything attached?” He nods and grins. “Thanks. Appreciate it. Glad there’s still some good folks.”
“Ah! Right, since you’ve been a good fellow.” He leans in. “Just a word of advice. There’s been some strange happenings…” He gives directions to an area nearby. “Just take care to avoid the area. People have been disappearing, and others have been hearing odd noises in the night near there.”
Pug acknowledges and continues on, informing Burr when they meet up. Burr immediately walks back off toward the danger zone.

Lavender, Pug, and Karla proceed to the apartment building while Burr heads off on his own. They climb through a broken window on the first floor into a room that looks like an explosion occurred within — everything singed and burned.
Lavender reaches behind the bed and pulls out a package wrapped in fabric. She unwraps it to reveal the shattered glass dagger. “And that’s that. Package delivered.”
“You still have the canisters on you?” She raises an eyebrow.
She receives the canisters from Pug. “I’m not sure about that. I need to bring these back and secure them.”
“Let’s work again sometime.” She hands over a card with an address. “Come find me here. I might have another lead. Or, if you need any help with figuring things out with those… ‘relics’. Any information you guys find out about those two relics would be information I’d gladly pay for.”
She nods. “Ah. Wait. As a signing bonus, and for a job well done.” She takes out a stack of bills and hands it over — totaling 100,000 SAU. “Good to hear it. Hope it keeps up that way.”
Pug asks Lavender if she would be okay with taking Karla, or if Karla would like to stay with Pug. “She was pretty useful in healing the damage from the fight. That was something new. I wouldn’t mind.”
Karla looks up, tearing up. “You guys… You guys are growing up so fast… Will your inept friend really be okay without my assistance…?”
She nods, gives a thumbs up. “It’s time for the baby birds to leave the nest. It’s been really tough, having to take care of you two for all this time. But it’s all worth it seeing you two become independent.”
By the time Pug looks back, Karla has already begun walking away with Lavender, talking to her.
Pug goes to catch up with Burr, heading toward the area he was advised not to go towards.

Summary
The two agents, having split up with their newfound allies, head toward the area. Walking for over an hour, the buildings grow taller and the fog hangs lower. The air feels thinner and colder. They venture into completely unexplored territory — more destroyed buildings, rubble, and destroyed cars, far more destitute than the abandoned yet structurally sound apartment buildings of Death’s Head territory.
Pug, warm enough in his jacket, watches Burr shiver in his blood-soaked gown with virtually nothing else. The two banter between each other, making jokes about cannibalism, and as it turns weird, they eventually awkwardly stop, walking in silence.
As the fog hangs down lower, they spot a light flickering in an alleyway. Approaching the light, they find a barrel fire with markings of a small hideout: a collapsed, broken tent, dirty towels and cardboard on the ground for bedding, and a duffel bag on the floor.
Burr approaches the duffel bag, squatting down and unzipping it. In the dark, lit only by the fire’s flickering light, he catches a glimpse of a wallet and eagerly grabs for it. Pug hears a metal twang snap. A metal trap springs and catches deep into Burr’s forearm, its teeth stabbing into his flesh and crunching down.
Pug’s alarm bells ring as he glances around for threats. Burr pulls on the trap, careful not to make things worse, and feels a chain snaking through the bottom of the bag, under the collapsed tent and cardboard, deeper into the alleyway heading left.
Before either of them can react, a crossbow bolt sprouts out of Burr’s upper left arm, the force staggering him. Burr recovers and begins stomping down on the bear trap, prying it open with his right hand and left foot. Meanwhile, Pug spots a brief glimpse of movement vanishing from a second story window in the building immediately opposite the alleyway.
Pug immediately sets off to chase down the crossbow user, dashing across the street. By the time he reaches the other side, Burr has finished untrapping himself, blood seeping out where the trap had impaled. Burr picks up the bear trap and his sledgehammer, venturing deeper into the alleyway to check where the chain leads.
Pug opens the door to the building — a destitute, abandoned residential building. He spots a staircase immediately to his left and elevator doors further down. He presses the elevator button. It does not light up. Holding his spiral knuckleduster knife in his right hand and the flashlight in his left, Pug ventures up the stairs.
He reaches where the sniper had been: a collection of tables pushed together with blankets covering some, right in front of the window. Empty cans, bottles, and a half-eaten bag of chips suggest the sniper had been equipped to remain there for some time. Following the way the discarded blankets had been skewed towards, Pug climbs higher. The dust on the stairs leading to the third floor is noticeably disturbed — a fresh set of footsteps continuing upward but not setting foot onto the third floor.
Following the footsteps, Pug reaches the fourth floor, then the fifth, then the sixth. The weight of his inventory and metal-plated coat wear him down as he ascends, getting winded. Eventually he reaches the roof, right after the eighth floor. The door opens onto a flat rooftop where the fog hangs so low it’s hard to see even a few meters ahead.
Hearing the tail end of a high-pitched whistling noise, Pug moves cautiously toward the sound. He sees a thin, pole-like silhouette. Approaching it, he confirms his suspicions: a length of cord going across and down the street. He unlatches his belt and hooks on. The line creaks and sways under his weight, straining, but he has a secure grip.
Pug takes a step off the 8-story building and puts his whole weight on the straining line. He begins to zipline across, the line bowing and swaying, wind chill against his face. About two-thirds down the line, he hears a startling cracking and crashing noise from where he had come. The line goes slack, losing its tension while he’s in the air.
Initially aiming towards the 6th floor, Pug makes a split-second decision to not grab at the 5th floor as it passes by. He crashes through the window of the 4th floor. The glass shatters, turning into scattered glass and glass dust as he makes an ungraceful, tumbling landing. Bits of glass scatter all over him and get in his clothes. Aside from some scrapes and bruising, he’s remarkably okay. He hears footsteps from below, coming up. Pug hides in a darker part of the stairwell and waits.
Meanwhile, Burr rounds the corner and finds the end of the chain wrapped around the leg of a dumpster, padlocked. Disappointed at the lack of foes pulling him, he smacks the chain with the sledgehammer, crunching it and breaking a link. The bear trap and long length of chain are now free.
Burr hears a whistling noise above him. Something comes heading towards him — he doesn’t have enough time to properly react, only enough time to step out of its way as it crashes to the floor. The sound of glass shattering as his vision fills with yellow dust or powder. On his wounds, it tingles and burns. His eyes begin to have a burning sensation, watering up and obscuring his vision. He closes his eyes and stumbles back.
Something heavy but not particularly hard thunks into the back of Burr’s head and knocks his head forward. A plastic bottle, half-filled with liquid, rolls away. Opening his eyes, he sees an unmarked plastic bottle with the wrapper taken off, the liquid mostly clear. He pours it into his eyes — aside from a bit of grit and sand, it seems to be water. He successfully cleans out his eyes.
Burr then pisses in the bottle. He winds up the chain and bear trap, swings it around, and lets it fly forward. The bear trap hits the edge of a window, hits the pressure plate, snaps, then falls to the ground. He winds up again and lets it fly once more. The bear trap flies through the air, crashes through a window, and clamps down on something. He tugs and it drags something. He puts weight on it and begins to slowly ascend. He hears something cracking and snapping from above as the bear trap returns with a chair leg.
He hears a secondary crash upstairs. Heading up, even after the secondary crash, Burr continues up the stairs. Eventually ascending a few floors, he sees a silhouette in the dark on the stairs ahead.
Burr throws his bear trap forward at the figure while the figure jumps up into a dropkick. The figure kicks forward, directly onto the pressure plate. The trap clamps down onto the figure’s ankles as they kick, pushing the trap into Burr’s chest. The two of them begin tumbling down the stairs, getting caught up in the chains.

Summary
Pug runs down the rest of the building, breathing heavily and assuming Burr is performing one of his special tricks. He reaches the lobby where the cloaked figure leans over, panting, crossbow already raised and aiming towards him. Pug charges forward without hesitation. The figure backsteps and fires a bolt. “Get away..!” she shouts from beneath her shrouded form. Pug parries aside the bolt with his dagger, not losing any speed, and catches up in the immediate moment. In the same movement as the parry, he leaps forward with a flying knee to the face. She raises the crossbow to shield herself, but the knee strikes her arm, crossbow, and face. A mechanism snaps as she tumbles backwards onto the floor. Her cloak knocked off, her bloodied face drips from her nose. She is dazed, her weapon knocked away and broken a few steps away.
Pug asks if there are any more of her. She glares up, effortfully trying to sit up before tumbling back down. “Hah.. You invaders are all the same, aren’t you..? Violent brutes..” She glowers as Pug threatens to stab her unless she answers questions. Pug rejects her statement, stating he was just passing through, arguing that Burr’s search of the bag was reasonable and the attack was unprovoked. “Passing through.. Is that the best you can come up with? You tattooed fucks don’t even bother to come up with a good lie?” She says, resentment glowing. Pug asks indignantly if he looks like he has tattoos. “How am I supposed to know?! You’re geared up for war! Your pal is the one I was shooting at! No one else but you invaders dress up like that!” She seems to go from angry to confused as Pug defends their looks and coincidences. ”…So you’re not with those feral dogs?” She says. “I don’t know what they’re called. But they’re dogged and vicious. They’ve just been rampaging and raiding whatever’s in front of them.”
At Pug mentioning the tattoos that glow, she nods. ”…About a week ago, they came into our community. Raiding and pillaging everything in sight. No regard for any trade or talks.”
As the two chat, her eyes settle on a point behind Pug. Glancing over his shoulder, he hears the clinking of glass. He spots Burr, having come down from the building — not by his own volition. His unconscious form is held up in a kneeling position, held by his hair, by a similarly shrouded and cloaked figure, slightly taller than the one Pug fought. Jars of a yellow substance clink by her belt. A knife is held to Burr’s throat.
Pug tells the shorter woman to tell her taller compatriot to stand down, establishing that they are not the Stray Dogs. The taller one looks over at Pug, looks down at Burr, then looks over him some more. Before sheathing the knife and setting him down face down, crossing her arms.
Pug tells the two that they had heard about disappearances in the area and are here to solve it, asking if they know anything. “They’re killing people and pillaging buildings. I don’t know where you got your information, but this is far more than disappearances.” The former crossbow-wielder speaks up. Pug says they are here to help and save them. They are quiet. They glance at the broken crossbow, then at the state Burr is in, as Pug says they are lucky he did not kill her right then and there. “We’ll call it even, then?” She says. Pug remarks it sounds good and puts out his hand for a handshake, which is not accepted.
“So what can you do to resolve.. our problem?” She asks. “We have been trying to drive them out, but they’re… persistent.” She remarks, as Pug says his ideas are either to get them away or kill them.
Meanwhile, the taller one opens a small pouch and takes out a pinch of red dust, sprinkling it over Burr’s nose. Burr sneezes awake, his vision spinning, head aching, blood dripping from his forehead. Almost miraculously, Burr manages to stumble and carry his own weight, staggering to his feet.
Burr manages to glean information — these two are somehow not the enemy, and the Stray Dogs are in play and here in the territory. He begins to stumble to the right, without his hammer, heading towards the Stray Dogs. The two just watch him take stumbling steps forward. Pug asks for any base of operations the Stray Dogs may be in, or any information where they are at. Burr grumbles as he stumbles back into the building to stumble up several flights of stairs while incredibly disoriented.
Meanwhile, the sniper shares information: the Stray Dogs were nearby, deeper into the territory, having bunkered down in a building they took over. As Burr finally reaches back down the stairs, having retrieved his hammer, trap and chain, Pug asks if there is somewhere they could stay to rest up first before their assault on the Stray Dogs. This time, the taller one nods. She points behind Pug — towards the stairs Burr just finished coming down. They see Burr having given up and fallen asleep on the stairs. She takes out a small keyring, taking off a key, and tosses it towards Pug.
Completely miserable, the two ascend to the 16th floor. It takes Burr almost half an hour. He reaches the 16th floor where Pug is in front of a door — almost mockingly, the room is right next to the elevator. Burr drags himself over and hits the button. The button does not light up. The long way down tomorrow as well. Pug pretends to fumble with the key, taking forever to open the door. Eventually it is opened as Burr flops onto the bed, leaking blood. Pug duct-tapes his shoulder and forearm, hoping to seal the bleeding, and splints his wrist with a broken chair leg and more duct tape. The two drift off to bed, Pug clutching his shattered glass knife.

Summary
Eventually, the child wakes to the musky smell of dust and mildew, clogging the air. Awakening, he finds himself on the floor, dull wooden floorboards creaking below him. Looking around, the child finds himself in a long hallway. Scratches and scrapes drag across the floor and walls, as though a creature had torn its way through. The windows, laden with dust-filled curtains, hide the outside, the pitter-pattering of rain against the glass.
Along the child’s left is a portrait, yet without a closer viewing, it is difficult to make out. The child, spurred on by curiosity, takes a closer look at the portrait, whereupon surely it must contain the master of this manor. There, the child indeed finds the regal figure of a man, and yet, the man is not to be viewed. Holding a proper pose, the figure in the painting sits, poised and dignified. Adorned with a rounded top hat. Yet, the top hat rests upon naught. There is no face to be viewed, no master to be observed.
As the child sets his hands upon the portrait’s frame, as though to grip him back, roots begin to sprout out of the wood, clasping around his hands, intertwining between his fingers. A shuddering, tearing noise comes from down the hall. A figure unseen, yet known to be drawing near, from beyond the hallway’s stretching horizon. Crashing. Tearing. Churning. The sound of wood ripping and splintering, drawing closer.
The child stands his ground, clutching at the painting as the rupturing draws near. Eventually, a figure looms into sight. A regal, fine upper body of a man, hanging high up in the hallway, almost to the roof. Yet he bears no arms, nor head. The frocks of his suit jacket flowing down low. Far too low to be normal, until they rest upon the ground. Two wooden, creaking appendages reach out from behind its back to clasp at the walls, the roof, the floor. Its claws tearing through the wood, dragging it forward.
Slowly, the child begins to see beneath its waist, hidden in the confines, the shadows of its frocks. A ghastly visage. Sunken, nay, hollow eyes. Paper white skin dried and stretched upon a skeletal frame. The face of a man long since waiting.
”…You…” The entity speaks. “Have you seen… my Master…?”
The child replies that he has, as he lifts the painting to show the creature. It seems to quiver, rattling and shaking. Yet, from sadness or joy, it is unknown. “My… Master had such an unfortunate life…” “I still.. carry him with me… because no one remembers him anymore…” “I.. am the butler of this manor. Please… tell me… Can you see him? Can you see him well?”
The child remarks that he does see the Master, speaking no lies. The creature seems to quake and shiver, as tears begin to form at the edges of its sockets. “Is not the face of my master so graceful…? The eyes, so deep. The gaze, so noble…” It seems to look back at the child, no longer looking at the painting. “Thank you… I am starting to remember. The face of my master, reflected in your very own eyes..”
The creature reaches towards the child’s face. It reaches towards the child’s head, his vision dimming for a moment, as the creature pulls its appendage back. Leaving behind a clasped locket necklace upon the child’s chest. “For you… So you too.. May remember these bygone days…”
The child’s eyes grow hazy, as the vision stills and dissipates. Having spoken no lies, and having helped it to remember. The visage of the master will continue to be preserved by this child’s assistance. And may he carry that forward, to paint the City in that image.

Summary
Pug awakens, the clock on the wall reading 3:13 AM. Finding himself having not stabbed Burr, with a new necklace worn around his neck. Examining the necklace, Pug pops open the locket. Within, the image of the master, the same portrait he had seen in the dream. When checking the knife, however, within its fragmented edges, he feels as though he sees the soft pitter-pattering of rain as it lands against the glass from within.

Summary
Burr awakens at 5:30 AM, having not died in his sleep. A pounding headache remains with slight vertigo, but he finds he can still move and operate. His wounds sealed with duct tape appear to be holding fast. His left wrist remains splinted and unusable. Pug remains in top shape.
The two descend the stairs at a measured pace, Pug’s flashlight guiding them through the dark. Under no rush, they continue down, bickering back and forth about whether they have actually been productive — a conversation that goes nowhere, as their conversations tend to.
Following the directions given by the two guerilla fighters, they head deeper into the territory. The fog hangs lower in the cool mist of the early morning.

Summary
After a few minutes of walking, a metallic clatter draws the two toward an alleyway — a thirst for carbonation lighting their eyes. They race each other into the alley and find a group of four men in coats and jackets, one hooded, hunched over scraps of rags and clothing. At the sound of their approach, the men react quickly, drawing weapons. Burr tells them not to draw, as Pug brings up the soda and Burr asks about the Stray Dogs.
The hooded one speaks — there is a market nearby, and the Stray Dogs are finished. Their packleader, Bosco, “kicked the bucket.” As he lifts a finger to point the way, Burr spots a familiar pattern of tattoos on the back of his hand. Burr mutters ”…Punishment comes for everybody” and lunges forward, grabbing the man’s wrist and pushing back his sleeve to reveal more tattoos — reminiscent of the Stray Dog they fought a week earlier, though less densely inked. Burr comments on his lower rank. In the next moment, Burr’s body moves on autopilot, fueled by the rage he has been holding back. He pries the splint off his left arm and jabs it forward into the man’s neck.
Pug, witnessing the escalation, immediately draws his bayonet and stabs the nearest unsuspecting man in the neck. The blade sinks deep, severing the connection from spine to brain — an instant kill, the feedback of metal hitting bone traveling up the knife.
Burr’s splint crashes against the Stray Dog’s neck, which flashes a dull glow. The entire table leg fractures and shatters into splinters from the sheer force. The man spins and stumbles several steps away, his hood destroyed on his right shoulder, revealing more tattoos glowing and smoking. He breathes heavily, eyes wide. “What the fuck is ‘yer problem?!” Burr reaches out to Pug, who hands over his bayonet and draws the glass knife.
The Stray Dog charges, his forearm and fist tattoos glowing. Burr launches forward and stabs the bayonet downward directly into the man’s throat, paying no mind to the incoming attack. The blade sinks to its hilt against his spine. The man’s outstretched fist grazes the side of Burr’s head — tattoos glowing and smoking. Burr tears the blade out through the side of the man’s throat, flinging blood toward the remaining two men as the Stray Dog violently stumbles.
Pug follows the path of the blood spray, dashing forward in the exact moment Burr completes his maneuver. He drives his glass dagger up from below, sinking it under the second man’s sternum directly into his solar plexus. The knife sinks in without effort — like slowly slicing a knife through paper. The man seems unable to react. Pug yanks the knife out and moves to flick off the blood, but notices the blade is clean. The man has no stab wound. Yet his body was definitely impacted — his mouth hangs open in shock. Pug kicks him backward and he falls limply, crashing into the third man, whose pipe clatters to the floor as he catches the body.
The fight concludes. The hooded Stray Dog keels over, having clutched at his throat. The man Pug stabbed still breathes — limp, mouth hanging open, blood beginning to drip from his nose. Pug observes his glass knife and sees nothing different.
The third man, the one who dropped his pipe, protests: “I-I’m not a Stray Dog! Please..!” Burr checks his sleeves, neck, and elsewhere — no tattoos. The man does not know who the Stray Dogs are, had simply been trying to survive alongside whoever would tolerate his company. Burr tells him he is disgusted, then tells him to go. The man runs off, incessantly confused.
Pug tests the glass knife on the dead Stray Dog’s leg. The blade pushes up against the fabric of the pants but cannot cut through — not even the cloth yields.
He then walks over to the catatonic man and pushes him onto his back. Unceremoniously, he sinks the glass blade into the man’s forehead. The knife stops at the hilt, yet no wound appears where the blade enters. On close inspection, Pug spots something in the man’s pupils: the pitter-pattering of rain against the inside of his eyes, occasionally lit by flashes of lightning in a distant cloud. The knife resists wiggling, as if stuck somewhere within. Pug pulls it out — no wound on the forehead. The visions in the eyes remain. Blood begins to drip from the man’s ears.
Pug stabs again, pushing the blade into the man’s neck. No change. As he withdraws it, the rain against the inside of the man’s eyes grows stronger — visible droplets striking the back of his pupils as though they were windows. Lightning intensifies. The pupils begin to fog with clouds. Blood wells up like tears at the corners of his eyes, dripping down the sides of his face.
Pug glances at the locket on his chest. Within it, he sees the face of the master of the manor — the man he just stabbed.
Pug goes around looting the bodies as Burr walks over and curbstomps the catatonic man, ending his life. The man’s face disappears from the locket. Before Burr smashes the man’s head in, Pug checks his eyes — now dull and void, empty of any rain or thunder.
In total, Pug finds three wallets, each containing an ID and some money — 13,000 Ahn altogether. From the Stray Dog, he recovers a bronze chain bracelet and a bronze ring. Pug puts the ring on briefly and feels nothing. He gives both objects to Burr, who dons the ring and bracelet. Burr returns Pug’s bayonet. The two then head toward the market the Stray Dog had pointed them toward.

Summary
The two eventually wander onto a street of once-shops, their storefronts closed with iron gates and shuttered windows. One has already been broken into — clattering sounds come from within. It is a small grocery store. Walking past the powered-off metal detectors, they peer inside.
Several flashlights shine toward them from the darkness. “Oi! Who the fuck are you two?” Burr instigates back. The voices claim affiliation: “Hell fucking yeah we are! You ‘eard of us? Terror a’ the District 22 Backstreets?” Stray Dogs. Burr drops his hammer and charges into the dark, the flashlights trying to track him as he vanishes behind shelves. Pug takes the opening, ducking into the darkness on the opposite end.
Burr hoists a shelf and heaves it toward the light sources. “CATCH MOTHERFUCKERS!” A purple flash illuminates the dark as the shelf is smacked aside, crashing into another. “Fuu.. Loosen up, boys! Let’s have some fun!”
Pug charges forward and wraps an arm behind the yelling man — the largest of the three — stabbing his glass knife into his kidney from behind. Once, then twice. There is resistance, far more than paper, but the blade still penetrates. “Gh- Sneaky lil’ fucker..!” The man grabs Pug and slings him forward. Pug crashes into a shelf, his armor mostly protecting him from the force, but he hears the sound of glass shattering. Peering down, he finds the glass blade gone, only the handle remaining. His eyes drop to the locket — the man’s face now appears within it.
Burr charges the same Stray Dog. Heat emanates from his bronze ring. He accepts the energy flowing from it and punches forward, feeling the air resistance around his fist give way. The strike slams into the man’s stomach, creating a resounding impact. Tattoos glow brightly beneath his shirt. “Kgghhh..! Haha..! You’ve got some gusto, punk!” Burr feels a red-hot soreness around his finger, his arm aching as though overexerted.
The other two Stray Dogs charge Burr immediately after, fists glowing. Burr attempts to redirect their punches into each other. He pushes one fist off to the side successfully, but as he reaches for the second, a cracking noise rings out — a punch connects directly with his nose, knocking him backward several meters. He stands, slightly dazed, and finds his nose perfectly fine. On the floor in front of him lie the shattered remnants of his bronze chain bracelet. “Huh, pal wasn’t jokin’ saying he offed one of us, huh?” one of them comments.
The larger Stray Dog pushes himself off the shelf he was punched into, hands in his pockets, tattoos still emitting light. The other two crack their necks and loosen their joints. Burr takes the bear trap from his back, unchains himself, wraps the chain around his arm, and clamps the trap down onto it to hold it in place.
The larger Stray Dog turns away from Burr and peers into the darkness where Pug had been thrown. “Don’t think you’re off scot-free, backstabber.” Pug stances up and draws his railroad spike twisted knife. In the darkness, even more than the man’s glowing tattoos, Pug’s eyes hone in on the occasional glimpse of lightning flashing within the man’s eyes.
Burr charges his opponent and swings upward from below, channeling the ring’s energy into an uppercut that strikes the man’s sternum and lifts him off the ground. His chain necklace shatters as he flies backward into a shelf. Burr’s ring overheats — a burning sensation around his finger, his veins bulging, his right arm redder than it should be, aching as though a migraine were localized to the limb. He ducks under a follow-up punch, spins, and lands a strike to the man’s arm without the ring’s energy. The man smiles slightly, then spins on one leg — his other leg glowing — and drives a kick into Burr’s right arm. Several links of chain explode outward. The bear trap falls to the ground in two pieces. Burr is knocked onto his back, his arm aching, something feeling as though it may have minorly broken within, though he retains function.
Meanwhile, the larger Stray Dog dashes at Pug, legs and right arm glowing. “I’ll end you!” Pug ducks under the fist, narrowly avoiding the strike. The man spins, tattoos glowing at his waist, and redirects his momentum into another attack — punching a shelf instead, striking nowhere near Pug. Pug drives up from below, aiming at the man’s chin. The man begins to move his head out of the way, but then pauses as if unable to move — a sound of creaking wood, scraping and crunching, echoing in Pug’s head. Pug’s railroad spike knife strikes the base of the man’s chin. A metal chain pops and explodes off the man’s chest as he reels backward, nose beginning to bleed. “Kghh.. Fuck.. The Hell was that…?”
Pug gives him no room. He charges, firing a ballistic knife at the man’s face. The man ducks it, his tattoos glowing as he throws a kick forward — the wind pressure whistles past Pug’s head as he skirts past. Pug launches upward with his spiral dagger, aiming for center mass. The man twists to backstep, his tattoos glowing brighter toward his chest, dimming elsewhere. Lightning flashes in his eyes. For a split second, his focus wanes and the tattoos dim. Pug thrusts forward. The dagger embeds itself in the man’s chest, drilling against the bottom of his sternum before plunging into the solar plexus.
The man glances down at the blade in his chest, then back at Pug. He grins. “Got you, fucking rat..!” He grabs Pug’s collar with a glowing arm and lifts him. His other fist glows, two rings on his fingers beginning to shine. The lightning in his eyes intensifies — from this close, Pug sees the water droplets striking the back of his eyes. Blood begins to drip from the man’s eyes. His grin grows.
“Special move..! PUNCH!”
He strikes upward. His head swings down and into his own fist. His head explodes. His hand is missing, the fractured remnants of his forearm bones poking out. He collapses to his knees. Pug checks himself, then checks his knife — the glass blade has reformed. He stands there, covered in blood, in awe.
Behind him, the fight continues. Burr grasps a broken half of the bear trap, considers it, then tosses it to the floor and opts to go in barehanded. He charges and launches into a spinning back kick aimed at center mass. The Stray Dog’s legs glow as he steps forward into the hit. Burr’s leg catches against his chest with a satisfying thud — the chain on the man’s neck rattles and strains. The man grabs Burr’s ankle. “My turn, pal.” He pushes Burr’s leg up, half-jumps, and delivers a full-body dropkick directly into Burr’s chest. Burr rockets backward, the breath knocked out of him, his ribs straining and cracking as he tumbles down the aisle. Eventually he stops, struggling to breathe. He manages to gasp out: “You.. hit like a bitch..!”
The Stray Dog turns and sees the larger man’s blood-splattered body, half-illuminated by a rolled-over flashlight. ”…What the fuck?” Pug taunts him, asking if he wants it next. “No. Not really. Want to call it here?” Pug did not expect him to stop the fight. ”…You attacked us.” Pug explains they were looking for the Stray Dogs and their hideout.
“Well. You found the Stray Dogs. Or what’s left. Bigmouth there wouldn’t shut up about ‘em, despite us bein’ the ones fucked over by ‘em.” Pug asks what he means. The man explains: they are of Bosco’s pack, and Bosco is dead. The pack scattered after his death — they have no connections back and cannot hold territory while stranded. When Pug says he appreciates the information but this only ends one way, the man replies: “Really? You got someone hangin’ over your head too? Tough shit, then.”
A negotiation follows. The man offers full information in exchange for walking out alive, along with the Stray Dog Burr had knocked unconscious. Burr wheezes out a yes. Pug agrees.
The man delivers his information: the Stray Dogs came in with six packs. Bosco — dead. Rocco, Marco, Vito, Valentina, and one other whose name he cannot quite recall — Mario or Marius. He estimates around fifty members per pack. Half of Bosco’s packmates split off to search for the other packs and rejoin. This man is through with it. As for strength: Valentina is the strongest, no doubt — a legend even back home. Marco is next, a big up-and-comer — notably, a volunteer, not conscripted like the rest. Rocco falls somewhere after Marco. Vito is the weakest, a fatass living it up. The unnamed sixth packleader is somewhere between Rocco and Vito in strength. Those with strength show it off, the man explains — if this Marius has not made waves, he does not have fangs to bare. As for tattoos, most got their ink back home. Some received custom work from a shop nearby — a couple-story building with a massage parlor or something below it. Each Stray Dog is supposed to have their ink maintained by an assigned Tuner, but theirs disappeared after Bosco’s death. The man does not know how the circuits work, only that they work.
Pug tells him this place is off limits. “Capiche. I’m out of ‘ere. Hope I don’t run across any of the other strays, don’t know how a dog without a leash is gonna act, y’know?” He nods. “Same to you. Hope to see ‘ya never.” He picks up the unconscious Stray Dog and leaves the market.
Pug shines his flashlight over Burr, slumped in the corner. The damage is extensive. His left forearm now has an odd bulge that looks eerily close to having something poking out from the inside. His right arm is red, swollen, and looking on the verge of bursting — the finger with the bronze ring still lightly glowing, the smell of burnt flesh filling the air. His outfit has been eviscerated from the force of the kick and subsequent tumbling. A clear indentation of two bootprints marks his chest, and his chest does not appear to curve the way it should. His left leg carries heavy bruising around the ankle, along with bruising and scrapes all over the rest of his body. The duct tape has come off, his wounds reopening — the glass shard cuts bleeding again, his arm leaking blood from the previous day’s wounds.
Pug finds a blue plastic tarp and covers Burr in it. He stabilizes him with duct tape to keep him from moving around, then heads out to find help.

Summary
Pug sets out from the grocery store in light rain to find help for Burr. He backtracks through the Backstreets, retracing his steps toward the alley of the first Stray Dog ambush. He spots a group of six men — half of them carrying large backpacks, all of them in ponchos or hooded coats — and approaches. The three without packs step forward, hands ready at their weapons. He asks where a doctor might be found. “No idea. Just passin’ by, pal.” They let him pass.
He wanders to where he and Burr were ambushed, then, on a hunch, returns to the campfire barrel with the duffel bag. A man warms his hands there. Pug asks about a doctor; the man stammers, then admits he knows a spot. He leads Pug down an alley, into the lighter, higher fog, and to a basement door marked with a cross in blue paint.
Inside, a dingy waiting room. A man sits in a splattered white apron and a surgical mask. Pug explains he has an injured friend and needs a doctor brought to him. The doctor grows wary when Pug says he belongs to no group but is against the Stray Dogs, then pales when Pug brings up Bosco. “You got any idea what they did to the folk ‘ere ‘cause of that fuckup?” Pug argues that no one else is standing up to the Stray Dogs, and that the doctor would want them gone too. The doctor explodes: “Out! Get out of my shop!” Pug leaves, thinking the man a coward, and continues his search.

Summary
Burr lies beneath the blue tarp, fighting to breathe, unable to move his arms. The pain flashes through him as figures enter the store, take things from the shelves, and leave. Group after group passes through, looting. Far down the aisle, he hears the sound of flesh ripping and tearing. “Hoohh.. Good one, this one is, aye.” “W-What happened to ‘im..?” “Doesn’ matter, does it? Yank ‘is guts quick, and let’s get out of ‘ere.” They harvest the dead Stray Dog. By the time the passersby finish, every flashlight has been retrieved, and the store falls into total darkness.
Burr’s consciousness fades in and out. Then he hears footsteps again — not stopping by the shelves this time, but coming directly down his aisle, toward him. Sharp, pronounced clacking. Dress shoes. The rustle of flowing clothing as the figure stops above him. Burr cannot lift his head to look.
“Mmm… Pitiful..” The figure speaks almost to itself. Burr mumbles what shittalk he can. He asks if they are some kind of god, showing up when he is dying. “No. I wouldn’t say so, at least. Just.. someone that arrives before the bell rings.”
Burr jokes with the figure as though with Death, an old friend. The figure asks him: isn’t it unfair? Burr answers that it is all unfair, yet as everyone is dealing with the unfairness, it is fair in its own twisted way. The figure counters — not everyone deals with the same struggles. Those who obtain power without merit, who wield it freely without tasting defeat. Is life unfair to them too? Burr only wheezes in reply.
“For someone unlucky, living in an unfair, yet fair world. Wouldn’t you like a little help to balance the scale?” Burr speaks of making the unfair fair, and that he does not mind becoming a monster to do what he needs to do. “It’s good then, that I got here before She did.” Burr asks who She is. “The one that tolls the bell.” For now, She waits. She will not visit him, not yet.
“In the meantime, you’ve got some work to do. Rather, we’ve got some work to do. I’ll visit again, get well soon.” The figure places a hand on Burr’s forehead. A buzzing, static-like feeling washes over him, like when a leg falls asleep and will not move — a cold, numbing sensation spreading through his body, akin to television static. His vision dims as he hears the figure walking away, the crisp clatter of footsteps vanishing into the distance.
